en: Having bowed to the beloved of Śrī, whose head is adorned with white radiance, to the Lord of Gaurī, to the state of the Guru, and to the lotus-dwelling one, we shall recite the *Padakārikāratnamālā* composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya,
which possesses most beautiful characteristics and has indeed been revealed by the Teachers of the words.

The sequence of words, the marking of word-boundaries, the observation of elisions (*visarga*), and the characteristics of final consonants (*nānta*) will be explained; however, the loss [of vowels] is restricted to single-syllable words.
Vowels lacking the phonemes *ṛ* and *ḷ*, or those that are not *ya*, are not subject to this.
The tenth is to be known by its censure (nindu); from the visarga, there are twenty.
The digit three is the *kuṅkuśa*; the side is the letter *u*, which has marks on both sides. Wherever the mark of the near-three is clearly manifest here, [it is to be understood].

The definition of the *padas* has been declared, and immediately after that, the definition of the *velās*; then the five *vārgas*, the five *ūrdhvarephas*, and the ten *ubhayāṅkuśas*— this is the characteristic in the Veda of the Vājasaneyins.
The observation of the five visargas is by means of the letters ending in the *varga* groups;

likewise, there is another *repha* (the letter *ra*) and five [others], as well as the parrot (*śuka*) in the two fives; and the mark of the flowing visarga belongs to the *varga* groups and the consonants (*hal*) in sequence.
Likewise, those with the *visarga* situated in water (the vowels) have the characteristic of being attained by the letter *ha*.
Similarly, having seen those without a fixed time (*avelā*), one should strike them in sequence as they reside in *la*.
For the letters ending in *na*, there is no *na*; and for the consonant groups (*vargāṇām*), the *hal* [consonants] follow their respective order.
Likewise, the *ūṣman* sounds, excluding the internal *repha*, in their proper order;
and for the five [groups], there are two wings: "śukī" and "pāriśvatī.
This is the full, intrinsic characteristic of the seven feet at the end of the *gaṇas*.
He was a knower of the investigation of all scriptures, possessed of virtuous conduct, devoted to austerity and meditative concentration, endowed with constant meditation upon his guru,
a knower of the true essence of the meaning of all the Vedas, and possessed of a radiance equal to ten million suns.
I, named Śaṅkarācārya, who know the discernment of all scriptures, am the pure sovereign of all mantras; and I shall proclaim the *Ratnamālā*,
having bowed at the two feet of Viśvanātha, who is united with Umā.
From the belly of the Lord Śrīkānta emerged Brāhmaṇa, Bhāskara, Vyāsa, and Jaṭātman;
from the great wish-fulfilling tree of the Yajurveda, there arose one hundred and one branches, the first of which is known as the Kāṇva.
This meritorious, purifying, and holy assembly of all mantras is equal to the best of all Yajus; it contains the verses,
the summaries, the Ratnamālā, and the Saudvaka.
Just as it is stated in the various branches [of the Veda] and according to the performance [of the ritual],
I shall indeed proclaim the *Ratnamālikā* in accordance with the Śruti, including the words, the euphonic combinations (*saṃdhi*), and likewise the elisions (*visarga*).
I shall now describe the sequence for those [mantras] ending in *nām*; it is calculated as follows:
for the mantra beginning with *iṣe tvā*, there are exactly thirteen word-units (*pada*), one wrapping (*veṣṭana*), and three releases (*visarga*).
"Be strengthened by the two [verses] beginning with *caturdaśyām*; there are two [verses] for the choosing (*vṛta*) and seven for the releasing (*visarjanāḥ*).

For indeed, the eleventh is fixed (*dhruvā*) in this [context]; one [verse] is for the *ekavṛtri*, and four for the *visrujin*. There are ten for the chest (*daurasi*), one for the *vṛtri*, and there should be four for the *visargāḥ*."
Fifteen [syllables] for the *ṛca*, twenty-four for the *anuṣṭubh*, twelve for the *deva* (triṣṭubh), and twelve for the *vṛddhi*; three *sargas* follow in succession.
Twelve for the *deva*, twelve for the *vṛddhi*, and three *sargas* follow in succession.
"O God, twelve," "and two," "threefold creation," and "the others" in sequence;
these thirteen are for Sāvitrī, four for Viṣṇu,
"fivefold," "O Agni, Lord of Vows," and "the vow" as a single binding.
Who yokes you? The tenth [verse], two *visargas*, as in the case of the two words;
"the *rakṣas* is burnt away" on the twelfth; four [syllables], eight *visargas*;
the seven-word [verse] belongs to the gods; the sevenfold *vṛtti* consists of *visargas*.
On the seventeenth day, however, there are Viṣṇu, tvā, trayovṛt, and pañcavisrutāḥ;
on the twelfth day, [the verses] juṣṭam for Agni, vṛt once, and one visarjana;
[then] dṛm̐, hantā, vaṣṭṛ, duryyā, pyolaśīm, and one vṛtti-visarjanā.
"You two are the purifiers; you are twelvefold and fourfold;
the divine waters are fourfold and twelvefold; you are fivefold and fourfold;
Indra [chose] you twentyfold; you are threefold, fivefold, and fourfold, [you who are] the releases."
For the divine rite on the twelfth day, there are three for each of the two [periods] of the morning;
likewise, on the thirteenth day, there are three with "śarma asi"; on the fourteenth day, five; then on the eleventh day, one with "adri rasi" and one in the east, and likewise four.
"O Agni, you are the breast"—this [verse] consists of eight [syllables]; there are two *veṣṭana*s;
becoming three, they make fourteen; the *bṛhat-grāvan* has four; the *kukakusi* has four, one, and nine; then ten, two, two, and two *visarga*s follow thereafter.
On the tenth day, Varṣavṛddha and four [others], Vṛtra, Visruk, and Apahata; on the fourteenth day, Vṛṭvaya is said to be the sixth;
and on the thirteenth day, Dhṛṣṭi—these three are the elders who perform the dismissal (nisarjana).

On the twelfth [verse], "dhruvam asi," there are thirteen [syllables] and one *visarjana*; on the fourteenth, "agne brahman navapadā viśvābhyaḥ tvā," there are fourteen [syllables]; on the eighteenth, "ekaṃ pañca ca dhiṣaṇā," there are two *visarjana*s.
On the eleventh day, one [verse] beginning with *dhānyam*, two ending with *vṛtra*, and one as previously stated;
on the fourteenth day, one beginning with *prāṇāya tvā* and three ending with *vṛtra*;
and on the fourteenth day, one beginning with *vedo asi* and likewise those ending with *visarga*.
I pour together nineteen, two, seven, and those that are renowned;
this [is for] Agni and the sixteen-fold [stoma], three, six, and the Visarjana-s; the sixteen-fold, the Agniṣṭut, the skin, and the two increases become the seventh.
Do not fear; there are fifteen [verses], one [verse] is the emission of rain, and likewise the fifth is the fivefold sacrifice;
from the fifteen, twenty-four have flowed forth as the armor of the earth, ten, six, one, and yet one more.
The twenty-fourth [letter] goes to Vraja; from Vṛṭvau, there are six and one.
Apāruru occurs on the fourteenth day; the two Prāṭvau are known as Visrugokanān.
Having reached Yatreṇatvāṣṭa, the twenty-eighth is proclaimed as Veṣṭanau Ṭvau.
In ancient times, Kūra [composed] eighteen [verses]; Pañcanān [composed] five; two [others composed] six;
Aniśita [composed] sixteen; Āśyā [composed] one with six *vṛc*s;
Visruta [composed] five; the Ādityas [composed] ten; and Pṛdaku is said to have [composed] one for each of two [hymns].
O Agni, with the straight ladle, there are twelve and three; six and [the] *visrug*;
as for the eleventh, "thou art splendor" (*tejo 'si*)—that is one and indeed another single [verse]; "that which is thy breath" (*yas te prāṇaḥ*) is twenty; and the fifth consists of three *nān*.
Thus ends the first chapter in the *Padakārikārthamālā* on the *Vājasaneyisaṃhitā*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
Now begins the second chapter.
There are twenty-two [offerings] for Kṛṣṇa; five are for the Vṛṣṭi-libations;
one is for Aditi on the eleventh day; three are for Indra;
and likewise three for Bhūpati on the thirteenth day—this is called the Vṛṣṭi-group.
For the sacrificer, there is one *vṛt* with seventeen [verses], and seven streams; for you, the invoker of the sacrifice, with nine, likewise in two enclosures;
"Thou art the kindler" (*samid asi*) on the twelfth day, and four for the one who has performed the *vṛt*.
On the eleventh day, two [verses] of Ūrṇāmradas were recited, and four of Ghṛtācya; on the eighteenth, one [verse] of the same, and one more;
on the fourteenth, the Dhruvās settled, consisting of one Trivṛt and one that is not final.
On the fifteenth day, O Agni, there is victory and the discharge of weapons; on the twelfth day, the clarified butter is not spilled, and likewise it becomes singular from the one;
on the seventeenth day, there is the earth, and likewise the fifth is chosen as one.

O Agni, there are eleven [deities] for the two [sacrifices], and for this [rite] there is the Sviṣṭakṛt; the god [is invoked] with water, and there is one release. Here, at the Pitṛyajña, on the eleventh day, among the three, there is a choice of two releases.
There is one *upahūta* for the eleventh [day], and one *visarjana* for each;
having been invited eleven times, one should listen to one [verse] in three steps.
May these twenty-four [verses] enter; six are the *vṛt*, and seven end with the word "one."
O God Savitṛ, this is the twelfth [verse] for you; the *visarjana* is on the thirteenth day. On the fourteenth day, there are six *vṛt*s and four [verses];
likewise, Bṛhaspati [recites] the fifteenth [day], as well as one *vṛt* and the seventh.
With the formula "mitrasya tvā cakṣuṣā," he takes it up separately with seven steps;
for Agni, there is the *ṣoḍaśī* with one *vṛt* and six *visarjanas*;
on the thirteenth [day], there is one *vṛt* and two *visarjanas* accompanied by the utterance of *svāhā*.

Indra’s: you are not one; two *vṛt*s, two terminations, the out-breath and in-breath—these are my twenty. From the two *visarga*s, there is one non-duality. This, O Agni, is your kindling; sixteen is called one *vṛt*.
In that seventeenth [section], there is one *devavṛt* and two *visarjanas*; in the *mano jyotis*, there are twenty and four *visarjanas*;
in the *agnīṣoma*, there are twenty-eight and four *keṣakanas*.

For the Vasus, let two [verses] for the eleven [deities] go forth; for the three Vṛtris, let the seventeen [verses] go forth amidst the Visruṣas; with six [verses], let them go forth for the Visarjanāyakas;
with twelve [verses], let the four [verses] for the Cakṣuṣpās go forth; let the six [verses] for the Asivṛts go forth.
In the *tantu* [offering] on the sixteenth day, there is one [verse]; three are for the *visarjana*;
eight parts are for the *saṃsrava*; twenty-eight, six, and seven; the eighth has one name; eighteen for Agni; ten for the *daṣṭi* and *āyuḥ*; five for the *brūka*; four for the *visruk*.
The *pañcadaśa* [stoma] belongs to Agni; there are three *ekaviṃśa* [stomas];
the *utpuruṣa* is the twenty-fifth; and there are six, eight, and one.
On the fourteenth day, there is the *devāgātu*, and there are four *visruta* [stomas].
The renowned [sacrifices] are Varāhīnavadaśastra (seven),
Kasta (one), Vimuc (eleven), Indribhirvisrugni (two),
Veṣosyupa (twelve), Dvisruk (four), and Cakranān (four).
The twelvefold [stomas] obstruct the four rites; by means of the two [stomas], one overcomes the two with splendor;
the two [stomas] are enveloped, and likewise the four are spread out;
the threefold [stoma] is the praise of the sacrifice, and the fifteenfold [stoma] is the single enclosure.
In heaven, Viṣṇu’s [sections] are nine, ten, two, six, and one;
from this, there are nine, and likewise two, two, and three;
on the fourteenth day, there are three sections and six that are well-known.
On the twelfth day, O Agni Gṛhapati, there are five *vṛtti*s and three *visargakas*; on the sixteenth day of the two [fortnights], there are two *vṛtti*s and three *sruc*s;
and on the fourteenth day of the wide Viṣṇu, there are four and one *visruk*.
Then, on the fifteenth day, [one should perform] one, two, three, or up to twenty-four; this is my ritual action (karman) with two or three [verses].
For Agni Kavyavāhana, there are ten [verses]; then four [are recited] with three [verses].
Those forms [occur] on the seventeenth [verse]: three, six, four, and one;
twenty-three, *namas*, *vo*, elision (*visarga*), eleven, and one; *udāyuṣā*, twelve, two; *vṛdhe*, one, and elision, and one.
"Ten, two, eight, fathers, seven, one, and two; Visruk, carrying strength, twenty-two, one, seven, three, one"—
thus [ends] the *Padakārikā Ratnamālā* on the *Vājasaneyisaṃhitā*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
The second chapter is completed.
Now begins the third chapter: "With fuel, [one worships] Agni"—ten [verses], one [section], one [chapter], one [part], and one [sub-part].
To the well-kindled flame, [there are] seven steps; in two places, there is the word "sound" (*śabda*).
With nine fuel-sticks, one is surrounded; here, however, two are [surrounded]. O Agni, come to us with the tenfold oblation; in three directions, the streams flow forth.
"Bhūr bhuvaḥ svar" is the seventeenth; five are fivefold and six are well-known.
"Āyaṃ gauḥ" is the twelfth; two are twofold, four are fourfold, and one is without end.
It moves within by means of ten; in two it is increased, and in two it is low-voiced.
Thirty, eleven, and one again for two;
fourteen for the *agni-jyotis* hymn; six for "tvam eva" and the *sūrya-jyotis* hymn on the fourteenth day; five and six are released.
May he, in harmony with the god, bite three and four,
and likewise ten; may the god, in harmony, [bite] three and four as prescribed here for nourishment on the seventeenth day, and likewise eight for the two increases.
*Anamitram me adharāt* (the thirteenth), *ekavisrutaḥ* (the fourteenth),
*indraḥ paścāt* (the fifteenth), *visargāḥ pañca caikanān* (the five *visarga*s and the one *ekanān*),
and *daśabhiḥ samidassyoti*— of these three [sections], one is chosen.
In *upaprayantaḥ*, there are two *vṛtta*s and one *ekaka*;
in *agnirmūrdhā*, there are ten [syllables] and four *visarjana*s;
in both *ubhā vām* and *saptadaśī*, there are two *vṛtta*s and one *ekaviṣruka*.
This is your source: in the *ṣoḍaśī* [stotra], one [verse] with six emissions;
in the *saptadaśī*, here, four [verses] with seven [emissions];
and in the increase during the emission, "asya pratnā" [is used] with ten [emissions].
The *tanūpā* [section] has eighteen [verses], the *trivṛt* has seven, and the *visrug* has sixteen; in the *āgneyī* there is one for the body (*tanū*) and likewise by means of the *vṛtti*s;
the two [sections] possess vitality (*vayasvantau*), and vitality consists of eight; with three [verses] there are five *visrug*s, and likewise.
On the thirteenth day, Citrāvasu [performs] one; the Ekaviṃśatiruts [perform] nineteen; with Saṃpriya, nineteen; the seventh becomes one;
the two Ūrjas [perform] nineteen; and for Ūrja, one; likewise seven for the first.
Right here is the fifteenth; for two verses there is one *vṛkṣa* without distress.
"Upa tvāgne" occurs on the eleventh day; for two [verses] and three [days], the wheel has turned.
"Rājantam adhvarāṇām"—thus eight steps have been made.
"O Father, ten for us," "two," and "four are spread out"—
O Agni, you are our [portion] on the seventeenth [verse]; with two and eight here,
but the seventeenth is "the thread has shone forth," and three and six are spread out.
In the *ilā*, there are eleven; likewise, there are twenty-one *sruks*.
From the eight *somāna* and *svarana*, there are three *visarjanas*.
Another [set] belongs to *yos*; and on the eleventh day, there are four, seven, and one.
On the eleventh day, he was measured out with six *visarjanīya* syllables;
then, with nine [syllables] of the *mahitrīṇām*, one *vṛtra-hymn*; then "for they do not measure them" (*nahi teṣāṃ mā*), two *vṛt* [hymns], two *yoḥ*, and the *rathantara*.
For those sons are ten and three dismissals;
sometimes they are nineteen, two by two, and one is desired;
that [verse] of Savitṛ has ten syllables, one [has] five, and the Visrug verses have five.
From the eighteen *ṛṣis*, there are six *visargas* and one *nān*;
"bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ" is seen with ten, five *vṛc*s, and eight;
"narya prajāṃ" has thirteen, three, two, and one ending in *n*.
O Agni, Sovereign, on the fourteenth day, [recite] five [verses], then five and one;
O Agni Gṛhapati, on the seventeenth day, recite one; then three for Vṛc;
on the sixteenth day, recite four; and on the two [following] days, six.

For the Grahas, there are twelve [stotras], with two for each; for the Ṣaḍahas, one for each; for the Unnetṛ, fifteen; for the Praghāsins, four and likewise six; and for the Visrutas, seven, two, and four.
That which is in the village and that which is on the thirteenth day is called one *visarga*;
but in the *moṣūṇa* there are twenty-two, and three eights are called one.
In the *akan-karma* on the thirteenth day, from the three, four and one [are added].
With the *avabhṛtha* on the seventeenth day, there are seven turns and six full ladles;
on the fourteenth day, he enters upon three and one;
with nineteen [verses] he says, "Give to me," and then follows two enclosures.
The sixteenth [verse] is "annamīmadat" with two [verses]; four [verses] each for the next two;
the seventeenth [verse] is "susandṛśam"; four [verses] for the next two; likewise, "manonvāhuvā" with nine [verses]; "vṛcchaikam" with two [verses]; and two [verses] for the two "visrutau".
In the Ānīka-stoma, there are twelve verses; likewise, one [verse] with three *visrutas*;
ten again for the *pitaraḥ*; six *visargas* thereafter;
nine in the *varya-soma-vṛta*; and one in the three *visruṣ* of the *vṛt*.
In the seventeenth [verse], O Rudra, there are six syllables accompanied by a visarga;
and the seventeenth [verse] ending in "rudra" consists of two groups of two [syllables each];
with ten [syllables] comes "bheṣajam asi," and the wrapping should be on one side.
The *triyambaka* [verse] once; four and two *sruks*;
by this, O Rudra, sixteen; four, seven, and one for the *vājins*;
nine, ten, and two; five and one for the *vṛt*.
Or for three days with nine [verses] for the *vājins*; two [days] with this same [set]; nine [days] with those impelled by Savitṛ; two [days] with the two [verses] beginning "iṣṭanau";
then three [days] with the eleven [verses] beginning "kaśyapasya"; and on the eleventh day, one [day] with five [verses].
In this manner, on the thirteenth [syllable], one *visarga* is said;
for the sake of long life, there are ten [syllables], and in the thirty-third [verse] there are two *visargas*.
Thus ends the third chapter in the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā, composed by Śaṅkarācārya.
Now begins the fourth chapter: "Seventeen; we have come to this; four and six are spread abroad;
these waters are twenty-one; there should be eight in three places, and likewise one."
For the *viśvajit* consists of twenty-four [stomas], and one [is formed] by six; the milk of the earth is sixteenfold; from two [verses] seven streams flow;
twenty-two [are for] Citpati; one should bring [the oblation] from five [verses] with the *māṣa*.
Three on the thirteenth day for you, O gods; two on the sixth; but all indeed [are offered] with *svāhā* at the sacrifice. Nine steps from the mind; two are the spreading-out offerings (*visrugau*);
twenty-three for the intention (*kūti*); four are the wooden ladles (*vṛc-catusruk*).
On the thirteenth day, *viśvaḥ* and *devaḥ*, as well as four *visarga*s;
on the fourteenth day, those of the *ṛc*s and *sāman*s, from which five [syllables] three have issued forth:
*śarma asi*, *śarma aṣṭadaśaḥ*, one, and *vṛtriḥ* indeed.
The *nīvi* of Soma is on the fourteenth; likewise, there is one on the fifth.
On the eleventh, perform the *ucchrayasva*; there are three *visarjanas*.
From ten, perform the dance (*nṛtaṃ kṛṇuta*) with five *visargakas*.
On the eleventh day, there is the sacrifice to the gods; four [verses] are for two [deities], and those who are gods [are addressed] on the thirteenth day. Three are for Vr̥tra, nine are for Visr̥k;
Śvātra is for eight, Pīta for eighteen, Vr̥t for two, and Visr̥k for the twelfth day.
And on the sixteenth [day], from three and from five;
O Agni, on the fourteenth, you create from three and from three, one by one;
"punar naḥ" on the nineteenth with five, and on the fifteenth.

O Agni, you [are the master] of the vows on the eleventh day; likewise, grant one separately for each of the Vṛtris. And that which belongs to the thirteenth day consists of four Visarjanas. On the seventeenth day, may this Śukra [be offered] to you with three Visargas.
Of that [cycle], on the thirteenth day, three [verses] belong to Vṛc; two [belong] to Yari-cit, who is Manasvin;
on the thirteenth day, three [belong] to Visruta;
four [belong] to Mitra, who has fallen upon the eighteenth day; and from the three [days], four [belong] to Sarvadā.

That goddess [is worshipped] with the *ṣoḍaśī* [vowels] on the sixteenth day; two *takas* (the letters *ta* and *tha*) are prescribed for the fourteenth day. With the letter *tha* and one [additional element], there is a sequence of three in due order.
On the twelfth day, [there is] *ādityā*; *tvā* is at the head of the three, and there are two [elements] for this [group].
*asme ramasva* with nine; *catvāri ca* and *trayas tathā mā vayam* with eight; *aṣṭāviṃśatyā* with three; *pañcabhya ekakam* with seventeen; *te gāyatrā* with three; and *ṣaḍbhir yathākramam*.
Nine for us, and one for the *siśuka*; four for the *visrugas*, twenty-four for *abhityam*, and six for the seven *pajās*.
Eight for you, O *tvaṣṭṛ*, five for the three [groups] thereafter.

O Candra, on the fourteenth day, one [verse] is recited with a single breath; on the tenth day, two [verses] are recited as the body of austerity; and on the fourteenth day, two [verses] are recited in sequence, and then one, two, and one again.
Mitro naḥ caturdaśyām atha ca eka-dvā-ricaikanaḥ.
The *svāhā* [verse], the *bhrāja*, the fifteenth, three from the *trayas*, then two;
thereafter, O Agni, the *pari* [verse], the *ṣoḍaśī*, three, and one; likewise, one for the *pratipanthā*, the twelfth, and likewise one, which shall become two.
The skin of the twenty-four Ādityas is there; one [syllable] for the four, eighteen in the forests, two for that, two are desired for the bowstring,
the eye of the Sun in the twelfth, or one, and six for the emissions.
One should begin with *usrāvetam* on the twelfth [day], then four [verses] for each [subsequent day];
*bhadro me* with twenty-seven; then three [verses] for seven [days] and two [verses] thereafter; *namo mitrasya* with sixteen; then three [verses] for two [days] and the *vṛca* thereafter.
"Varuṇasyottambhana-daśa ca catvārīti ekaviṃśati-srajaḥ;
yā te dhāmāni-avadaśa pañca-catvāri ca ekakam"—
thus [ends] the *Padakārikā-ratnamālā* on the *Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
The Fourth Chapter;
now the Fifth Chapter:
On the fourteenth [tithi], the body of Agni [is worshipped] with two [verses] and likewise with three.
O Agni, there are eighteen [syllables] in the *janitra* hymn; one [is] the *eka*; four are the *visrutāḥ*.
May they be for us on the fifteenth day; four and three indeed.
Eighteen in the fire, and Agni; four and seven as one.
For the sake of long life, you [are addressed]; then eight [verses] from three [hymns], ending with one containing the word *vṛtra*;
"anādhṛṣṭam asi" [is recited] from eight [verses] and two from three; on the eleventh [verse], "satyam" [is recited] from three, and those [verses] containing *vṛtra* and *īryatāḥ* are employed.
That which is yours [is obtained] from twenty-four; immediately after three and six, there is the *am̐śu*; for you, O Hero, it is from sixteen; likewise, three from two;
O Āpyāyana, three from thirteen; and one from the two at the end of the *ekavṛt*.
On the eleventh day, with eighteen [verses] and with two and five; when Agni has departed, with eighteen again, four, and five;
on the twelfth day, the two enclosures for the path to heat according to the rule.
O Agni, there are twenty-five *vids*; for Indra, there are two *vṛts* and six *visarjanās*. Ghoṣa is the fifteenth; the *ṣaṭka* has ten *visruts*.
This twelfth [section] is heated; and from the two, there are four *catasruks*.
The Ekādaśī has four and five; the Brahmavani is fixed at one; then the Pañcadaśī has two; the Vṛc has three;
the Visruk has nine; and likewise ten with three and ten.
*Idaṃ viṣṇuḥ* is on the twelfth day; *ekaṃ vṛddhi* is likewise [on the thirteenth]; *irāvatī* is on the seventeenth; six [verses] are proclaimed for *vṛtriyas*;
and on the fourteenth day, at *devaśruti*, there are three *veṣṭabhas*.
The eighteenth [verse] has its own *goṣṭha*; the four [verses] have four [syllables] each;

"viṣṇornukam" consists of nineteen [syllables]; the fifth [verse] consists of five [syllables] with five [repetitions]; "visruk divaḥ" consists of twenty-five [syllables]; here, in two [cases], there are four [syllables] each.
The seventeenth [verse], *pratad viṣṇuḥ*, has three *vṛt* and five *visruk*;
on the eleventh day, one takes one *vṛt* and four *visruk* from the verse *viṣṇor arāṭ*.
With thirty-two [syllables], one takes three; indeed, there are four [syllables] less than one hundred and one.

This [section] consists of twenty-one verses for the destruction of spells (*valaga*), nine verses for the four [classes], nine verses for the *svarāṭ* [hymn], eight verses for the ninth [day], and one verse for the *ekaviśruta*;
there are ten verses for the slayers of demons (*rakṣohan*), two verses here with the *vṛti* meters, and then [the rest].
The *rakṣohan* [hymn] has twelve verses; the two *vṛddhi* [hymns] have four;
the *visruk* and *yava* [hymns] have eleven each; the three *visargas* have exactly three [verses];
and the two ending in *śūnya* on the thirteenth day have two and two [verses] respectively.
Three [verses] for Indu-dūtā; for us, three for Tvā; two for Visruk; one for Brahma-darśa; twenty-one for Eka-viṃśat; four for Catuṣṭa-ekatā;
one for Paritvā on the thirteenth day; and seven for Vṛt-saptaviśrut.
"Indra syū," "dhruvam," six, and likewise one;
then two verses beginning with "vibhūr asi," nine, five, and eight;
"uśig asi" on the eighth verse, six, and one with the *visarga*.
*Ṛtadhāmā*, *iti ca*, eight, four, *vṛccha-saptamaḥ*,
*samrāj*, *kṛśānuḥ*; from eight, four, *vṛccha*, in the sixth [section],
*samūhya asi*, twenty-four, four, and nine, *avi-sruk*.
*jyotirasya* with twenty-one; again with five, seven, and seventeen [verses] beginning with *agne naya*; then two by two for each pair;
then *ayaṃ naḥ* with nineteen; again with two, six, and three.
The god Savitṛ [is praised] in eighteen verses;

the Pañcaviṃśa [stoma] consists of two sets of fifteen; this [world] and I [are connected] with three; from four comes oneness; that which is your body is twenty-eight; and there are four and six manifestations.
I have surpassed the others; the twelfth [is] threefold, with two endings;
through the thread, twelve for the two Vasus, and one for Vṛtra; the fifteenth [is] for the six-fold protection, and then the triple for Vṛtra.
"Nine with ten, for this one; four, having cut off, the fifth"—
thus ends the fifth chapter in the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the *Vājasaneyisaṃhitā*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
Now begins the sixth chapter:
"The leader with twenty-seven," "Four with eight," "Those which are your abodes," "Nineteen," "With two," and "The four renowned ones."

The *Viṣṇoḥ karmāṇi* has nine [verses], the *trisargāḥ* likewise three; "That supreme Viṣṇu" has ten, and the two [beginning with] "With the *vṛti*s" have twenty-two; "Thou art surrounded" (*parivīr asi*) has one, and "The *vṛt* [verse]" has ten, [ending] with *avisruk*.
The *upavīta* [is performed] with seventeen [verses], then with two, then with six for two [sacrifices];
then the *revatī*s with thirteen, and one here with three;
likewise, with nine for Agni and Soma, and one for two [sacrifices] if they are increased.

Apām peru is the tenth; likewise, one [verse] for Vṛcīnasa, four for Sante, and one for Prāṇa on the eleventh day; then three [verses] for Vṛcīnasa; two [verses] for Ghṛtenāktau, ten for Paśu, and one for the Visarjanīya.
At the end of the chest on the thirteenth [syllable], there is one *vṛtri* which becomes *visrug*;
on the fourteenth, *varṣo* and *varṣī* occur with six *visarjanas* in two places;
*namasta ātā* occurs on the twelfth, while *vṛ* occurs once and *tra* likewise thrice.
The *devīrāpaḥ* [section] consists of ten verses; the *śuddhāḥ* [section] consists of three; the *vṛcaṣaṭka* [section] is otherwise;
the *ācaṃte* [section] consists of twelve; therein the *visarga* [section] consists of one;
the *manasta āpyā* [section] consists of twenty-two; in two [sections] there are six *visrug*s as follows.

The twelfth [syllable] is recited there as the emission (*visarga*); indeed, for each individual [syllable], on the eleventh day one should say "Oṃ, O herb, protect me" (*oṃṣadhe trāyasva*). On the two [days], the fourth [syllable] is likewise [recited].
This tenth day is proclaimed as the two emissions by means of the *akṣobhi* [mantras].

With clarified butter, [one chants] *dyāvāpṛthivī* (four syllables), then *vṛtrahan* (three syllables); then *sante manaḥ* (seventeen syllables), four [syllables for] *visruka*, one [syllable for] *ekadhā*; from the wind-impelled [state], with clarified butter, nine [syllables], then one [syllable], then *vṛtra* (three syllables).
Clarified butter (ghṛta), clarified butter-footed (ghṛtapāda), and Śavyā; for two [verses], vṛc; and three in sequence:
the quarters (diśaḥ), the intermediate quarters (pradiśaḥ), the sixteen-syllable [verse], nine, and eleven; Avisruk; O Deva Tvaṣṭṛ, nineteen, four, and three; Visruk.
Go to the ocean with twenty; then with two, the second [ocean];
at the end of the day with eleven, the emission (*visarga*) likewise with two;
twenty-two for the waters and medicinal herbs, and one each for the eleven.
On the fifteenth day, there are the *sumitriyāṇa* verses; with two [verses], there is the unification of the eighth and the first.
One should perform this from eighteen [verses] down to two, and that [applies] to the two as well.
And on the twelfth day, there are the *haviṣmatī* verses; the discharges are six and three respectively.
On the thirteenth day, [he offers] *agnervapa* to three;
on the sixteenth day, *amūryā upa* to six with the *visrugs*;
and on the eleventh day, *hṛdetvāmana* to two, here at the two *visargas*.
From the *Somarāja* [hymn], ten; from the *Catvāri-caturaikatā*, four;
from the *Śṛṇo*, twenty-one; and also from the *Ekavṛt*, seven;
likewise, from the *Devīr Āpaḥ*, ten; and two from the *Vṛt* on the seventh day.
To him [be it offered] for the gods on the ninth, and on two [occasions]; as for three, according to how it is performed; on the fourteenth, one or the fifth [verse], the *visruk*;
on the thirteenth, "O Agni, you alone in battles" (*yamagne pṛtsu*); one [verse] beginning with "vṛt," five [verses] beginning with *sukra*.
In the beginning, with twenty [syllables], two are declared in the five;
the mind and the impulse are sixteen; by three [is] the turn, and by three [is] the breath; ten Indras having gone, the Vasus are six, and the turn is beyond the distant realm.

O Soma, let your seventeenfold [stoma] be the Visarga; then from the two [Aṣṭakas], there are two Pañcadaśas, or four from the eight [Aṣṭakas]. Or, from the two [Aṣṭakas], there are two Pañcadaśas, or four from the eight [Aṣṭakas].
Do not fear; from three and from four [syllables], there is the seventeenth [vowel].
Prior to the fifteenth, there are four visargas;
O dear one, in the seventeenth, however, there is one and four in unity.
Thus ends the sixth chapter in the *Padakārikā Ratnamālā* on the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
Now begins the seventh chapter.
Sixteen [stotras] for Vācaspati; three [verses] for Vṛtrahan-viśruta;
twenty-two for thee, O Soma; likewise one [set], which became the fifth;
twenty-six [stotras] for Manas, with Tvaṣṭṛ as the fifth; and the fifth [set] in sequence.
The *dvādaśī* has twelve; the *upayāmagṛhīta* has four; the *ekatā* has one; that which is within them is eighteen; that which is from six is said to be seven and one;
the *āvāyo* has twenty-one; and from six there are indeed four.
The ninth and tenth [verses] are addressed to Indra and Vāyu; there are four [verses], and the seventh should be [the same].
"Ayaṃ vām" occurs on the thirteenth day; one or two [verses] are recited.
"Rāyā vayaṃ" occurs with twenty-one [verses]; there are three [sections], each with six [verses] in due order.
From the *yāvāṅka* [section] up to the sixteenth [day], there are three and two for this; as of old, nine, eighteen, sevenfold, and the twenty-one-fold;
these are yours, the three Āśvins, thirty, eight, and the thirteenth of the two.
The uncut [verse] is the eighteenth; two [verses] flow out into eight;
with the first, there are eighteen; with two, the fifth is a unity;
this Vena is the eighteenth; and five times eight are seven.
The mind is not the seventeenth; rather, through two and through six, [you grant gifts] to the donor.
This is your thirty-third; and the ten, the five, the ten, and the oneness—those gods who are eighteen and likewise the one triad—enter into me.
The Āgrayaṇa cup is first with seven [verses]; for two [days] there is *vṛc*, for two [days] *visruk*;
Viṣṇu and you on the fourteenth day; three [days] are for the release;
twenty-two [verses] for us, for the Brahman priest; three [days] with eight [verses] for drinking.
Twenty-one verses for Indra; "ya tvā bṛhat" with two [verses]; four [verses] joined with the gods;
"devebhyas tvā"; eighteen or fifteen; the "pañcavṛt" and the "ekaviṃśati-vikhyāta"; "mūrdhānaṃ divaḥ" with eighteen and one, or three, as a unity.

"Dhruvasi" is the twelfth; "yas tu trayaḥ" and "ṣaḍbhyaḥ" likewise [are two]; "avisruk" is the thirteenth; "dhruvam" is the fourteenth; "dhruve" is the fifteenth; "ekam" is the sixteenth; "vṛt" and "pañcavisrutāḥ" are the seventeenth and eighteenth;
"yaste drapsaḥ" is the twenty-fifth; and "catvāri" and "aṣṭaṣvirānuṣak" are the nineteenth and twentieth.
To Madhava and Mādhava on the fourteenth; this [is performed] once each.
To Indra and Agni eighteen times; with five [verses], Visrutāghāya;
to Agni nineteen times; with four [verses], Visruta, in sequence.
The ninth month, *carṣaṇī*, and one; five verses with the word *vṛt* are scattered.
"O Viśve Devās, come hither" [is the first]; the thirteenth [verse], two [verses] with the word *visruk*. "O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts," then two [verses]; six [verses] with the word *ekatā*.
The *marutvantam* [hymn] consists of fifteen verses; with four [verses], one reaches the end of the first [section].
Then there are three *padās* beginning with "for the vigor of the Maruts" (*marutām ojaṣe tvā*).
Following that is the *sajoṣāḥ* [hymn] consisting of nineteen verses, and then four [verses] for two [sections] of six each.
"O Great Indra, the twenty-fourth; nine, twelve, and one;
O Great Indra, who [is praised] with nine, two, four, and two"—thus [ends] the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the *Vājasaneyisaṃhitā*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
The seventh chapter is completed.
Now begins the eighth chapter:
[the hymn] for the Ādityas consists of twenty-one verses; then two for Vṛtra, and two thereafter.
The *yajña* [is addressed] to the gods; the twenty-seventh [verse], likewise nine from three, two for the cooked offering, O men, twenty for two, five for one, not ending;
the beautiful, beginning and ending with ten, for three, in five streams.
On the thirteenth day [dedicated] to Savitṛ, there are two or four [verses];

for the five [verses] beginning with "suśarmāsi," there are three; at the two times [of the day], there are four verses for Visruk, the son of Bṛhaspati; and there is one for the two [verses] taken together.
Beyond that, twenty-one [verses] are recited once;
O Agni, one [verse] for Vākpatnī; one for the Vṛddhi-sruk;
Prajāpati [is invoked] on the thirteenth [day]; there are five, nine, and eleven [verses] for the Visrutā offerings.
Hari is the destroyer of enemies; he who is the sixteen-fold god of ten, three, five, seven, and twenty-seven [verses];
O Keśin, yoke the twenty-two, the four, the four, and the four.
The *ātiṣṭha* [sūkta] consists of fifteen verses; it is held that one verse each belongs to the two [deities], Indra and Miṭdarī.
On the twelfth day, there are two *lau*s and two *visruk*s. Because [the deity] is not yet born, the eighteenth [verse] has four [padas]; the seventh is a *visruk*.
The twenty-fifth is *indraśca*, the sovereign (*samrāj*) is one, and four are renowned as *catvāri*.
*agna āyūṃṣi* is thirty-one; there are three *trisargās* and three *nāntakas*.
*agne pacasva* has ten syllables, while *veloḥ* has three and *visruk* has two.
The hymn beginning with "uttiṣṭhan" consists of twenty-nine verses; then three, thirty-four, and nineteen;
after the nineteen, the "daśrama" hymn has ten verses; from the six, four are taken out;
then "jātavedasam" has ten, and from the two, one is likewise extracted.
The *Citrandevānām* has eighteen verses; likewise, the *Vṛcat* has one verse in the sixth [section].
O Indra, the *Vinat* has three verses; from the *Śattri* [section], there are seven verses with a single unity.
The *Vācaspati* has twenty-five verses; the *Ṣaḍvṛt* has six verses, and the *Velā* is the seventh.
The *viśvakarmān* [hymns] are seventeen; four [verses] have a unity of four;
on the seventeenth [verse], O Viśvakarman, one is released by two [verses]; five [verses] are for Agni; and then there is the twelfth [verse] and the triad of fivefold movements.
With seventeen verses, he offered one for each of the *preṣas*; likewise, with twenty-five, he offered one for the *kakuhā*. With two [verses], the outpourings (*visruta*) of six were offered;
with twenty-one, he offered one for the *uśig* in the three outpourings through his stride.
Thus ends the eighth chapter in the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
Now begins the ninth chapter.

In the *prāṇāyāma*, there are eight *ṛc*s; in two [sections], three *ṛc*s each are increased; by means of *kratu* and *dakṣa*, seven [are added] to me; in two [sections], two are increased and there are two *visarjana*s; in the ninth, however, for the sake of the self (*ātman*), there are nine, and in two [sections], three *visruta*s.
On the fifteenth day, there are three *kosikatama*s;
then, on the fifteenth day, there are four *visruk* and two *paśya*s;
on the fourteenth days, however, there are two *drā*s, which would be four and two *visrutau*.
To the giver of life, [I offer] the fifteenth; likewise, two [verses] of the fifth.
Who has given to whom the sixteenth? And Vela one. Visruk four.
O Indra, twenty for us, four, three, and unity.
Dhātṛ obtained the sixteenth and four [others]; the seventh found [the hymn] with good cattle;
the seventeenth belongs to three [deities], or it is renowned among six;
that which you brought [is] the twenty-second, but three [verses] belong to the third [deity] and five [to the second].
We have twenty-two [verses] in pairs; here, O Sacrifice, two by two, and with three [more], you are seventeen; four are indeed fourfold;
for the King is wide; there are twenty-two; six indeed are the turns, and six are the renowned ones.
The face of Agni with twenty, or three, or two, or oneness;
nine, ten, and in the ocean, five and four;
the divine waters, twenty-three, three, and seven are they that flow forth.
Let the two tides, the tenth and the eighteenth, move;
let the fifth be a stream, and let there be fifteen emissions for you.
May the fifth become one who bestows much wealth, possessing sixteen [parts] through seven in six streams.
O Maruts, he whose [body] might be broken by ten, two, and six—[the earth is] one among eleven; likewise, speaking of four, there are twenty-three;
smell it, O One, the fifth is the cloud-shatterer.
In the *havyekāmya* [section], there are eighteen; then two for the two *veṣṭana*s;
here, twenty *ratī*s for two; then five for two;
thereafter thirteen for the *aganmatyā*s; then *virvisruk* [is] five, one, and ending with nine.
With twenty-nine [verses] for Yuvant; three [for the Pañcamas]; Ekatā [with one];
Parameṣṭhin with thirteen; seven [for the Catvāris]; four [for the Visrutas]; ten [for the Daśas]; and Indra and the Maruts—therein, one [verse] for Vṛtra with seven [Maruts].
Viṣṇu [is praised] with six verses; the *śipis* are tenfold.
Agni is the *damas*; for the *āgnīdhra*, there are five transverse verses.
Viṣṇu is the *āprī* at the eleventh; from three [verses], the eleventh is the *visruk*.

The Śukra, the Kṣīra, the Ekādaśa, the Catuṣṭoma, and the Saptaviṃśa; the Sadraha, the Prasapta, the Saptadaśa, and the Viṣṭuti; those two [the Pañcadaśa] by whose might [the rite proceeds]; the Pañcadaśin, the Ṣaṭka, and the four Ekatas.
"Devān," "divam," and "dvāviṃśaḥ" [are single words]; "visruk" [is a compound of] "vi" and "sruk"; and "catvāri" and "pañca" [are separate].
Thus ends the ninth chapter in the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the Vājasaneyi-Saṃhitā composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
Now begins the tenth chapter:

*devasavitṛ* has twenty-one [syllables], and those beginning with *dvābhyām*, *vṛd*, and *aṣṭavisrutāḥ* have sixteen; furthermore, *dhruvasadam* has five syllables, while *pañcavṛt* and *catuḥ* have four each.
On the ninth day, having placed [the vessel] in water, one should perform six enclosures in sequence;
on the fourteenth day, the essence of the waters with three [verses];
on the thirteenth day, the houses with strength with two [verses]; and on the fourteenth day, the four streams with three [verses] in sequence.
On the twelfth day, two are joined together; indeed, there are two increases.
Indra’s thunderbolt is twenty-eight, and three and four are placed below.
On the fourteenth day, the divine waters [are present]; three, seven, and one meditate together.
Within the *apsu* there are eleven; then three in each of the next three [sections] in sequence; then *vāta*, *vāṣa*, and *laśī*; then one; then two with six;
then *vātaram* with eighteen; then four, five, and one.
Javas has twenty-three syllables; Vājins, winners of the prize, has four, three, and eight; Visrutas has one and four;
and for the sake of the divine impeller (Devasavitṛ) on the fourteenth [syllable], three are proclaimed as Vṛtis.
Or rather, O Bṛhaspati, [grant] strength; O Indra, strength again and again. This [verse] has sixteen syllables, but it is called "one" and "two.
By means of nine [syllables], the word *devasya* is formed; there, four [syllables] are elided.
With nine [syllables] the steed wins the prize; there are four releases.
The *eṣas* should be the seventeenth, and four times four;
thus its nineteenth [verse] is formed by three and seven, as it were.
May they be auspicious for us in the *ṣoḍaśī*; three [verses] kindle the sixfold and the single;
therefore, O steed, the seventeenfold [stoma]; five and seven have been brought together; in every contest for booty, O you [gods], in the *ṣoḍaśī*; four [verses] with nine again.
With twenty [verses] for "āmā vājasya," and again with five for the two [verses] on the "vājinaḥ"; with ninety-three for the "vājinam," the fifth is the "viṣruk.
With eighteen for "āpaye svāhā," one ṛk is desired for six [verses].
Āyu with ten, Viśarga likewise with four;
Jāya, come! with thirteen, and Bhavan with three;
may these be yours among us: twelve, and three, and likewise three.
Homage to the Mother; with sixteen [syllables] and four dismissals, this [hymn] of seventeen [syllables] becomes the fifth on the fifth day.
This [verse] of nineteen [syllables] belongs to Vāja; there is a unification of two by means of three.
Of the *vāja* hymn: these [verses] are nineteen, four, three, and one;
on the seventeenth [verse], "O Agni, toward this... there are three; the fifth is the *vṛt*;
"King Soma for aid" occurs on the eleventh; and the *vṛt* occurs once.
O Lord, on the fourteenth day, one should worship Yama; on the thirteenth day, the two [deities] Visnu and Rudra; on the eleventh day, Aryaman, Bṛhaspati, and the Padas in succession;
and on the sixteenth day, Sarasvatī—or rather, the pair [of deities] and the pair [of Padas] as a unity.
Agni [is worshipped] with one, thirty-six, six, seven, and eight;
Pūṣan with thirty-six, five, four, two, and eight;
and Mitra with nine, thirty-four, seven, four, and one.
"Vasavaḥ, trayodaśa, akṣa, pañcacatvāriṃśati,
adā, veṣṭanā, daśamaḥ, evam, visruk, sapta, trayaṃ— thus, in sequence," so it is stated in the *Padakārikā Ratnamālā* on the Vājasaneyi-Saṃhitā composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
The tenth chapter is completed.
Now begins the eleventh chapter:
this twenty-fourth [chapter] for you, the seventeenth on the thirteenth day.
Those gods who are eighteen, fifteen on the eleventh day, O Agni, twelve on the twelfth; three and six are desired as one;
with the Upāṃśu and the twenty-first, one [verse] is to be cut away, and the triple-threaded [cord].
The *Apo devāḥ* hymn consists of sixteen verses; the second [hymn] has two verses, and the third has nine.
The *vṛṣṇa ūrmiḥ* hymn has sixteen verses, while three others are intended for the seven [verses].
The twenty-fourth hymn stands for the purpose [of the sacrifice], and the eighteenth consists of nine verses and is distinct.

The *saṃmadhumatī* verses are on the sixteenth [day]; on the eighteenth, there are two [verses] from the *vṛc*, five [from the *sanitṛ*], and three from the [eighteenth day] and seven [from the seventeenth];
then follow this [verse], the gods, the sixteenth [verse], and two *visargas*.

The Dāṣavas and Kurus [are associated] with the twelfth; the Visargas are sevenfold, belonging to Soma. O Indra, the splendor [belongs] to you; with ten [verses], there is one Visarga. For the sake of the sacrifice, O Indra, on the sixteenth day, the offerings are spread across five [days].
The *sadhamāda* [hymn] is the fifteenth; then four [verses] with ten [syllables];
then the *kṣatrasya ulbam* is the sixteenth; likewise one [verse] with two increases (*vṛddhi*);
then from *rujādrubākṣuṣādaśa* there is one [verse]; and *pravṛdvisrug* is one [verse].
The *āvirmarya* [sacrifices] are eighteen, as well as eleven and nine; from the *aveṣṭi*, there are sixteen others; three are the *vṛt* and *pañcaviṃśat-srutā*;
the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) is on the fourteenth day, and likewise the second [set] consists of four.
Fourteen toward the west, one curved, and four straight;
fourteen toward the north, one curved, three curved, and then on the seventeenth [line], five ascending and likewise four.
Of Soma, on the thirteenth day, there is one; and being the fifth, there are twenty-three of golden form;
two in the sixth [day], and of Soma, twenty-two, and two in each of the two, and one indeed.
Twenty-three parvans, three, seven, and one;
O Prajāpati, not twenty; two here with five;
O Rudra, that which is your supreme stride, a single binding on the twelfth.
For Indra, the *vajra* is the twenty-first; with three and five likewise;
"O Mother, O Indra, with twenty"; and for the two [verses], the first and second;
for Agni Gṛhapati, the seventeenth; two; and then two more.
The *haṃsaḥ śuciṣat* [is recited] on the eighteenth day; the twelfth and seventeenth are well-known;
the twenty-fourth, the third, and the fourth likewise;
the *syonā si* is on the fourteenth; and by two [verses], one [day] is otherwise.
He sat down with the eight verses beginning with *ghṛta*, three for the Veda, and the *abhibhūḥ* verse; one should bring the twelfth, the thirteenth, and the first;
you are Savitṛ on the ninth day; there are three [verses] and seven [verses] flowing from the seer.
Priyaṃkara consists of nine, Agni of three, and Trayas likewise; Agni Pṛthu consists of nineteen, and Catvāri-dvādaśa becomes twelve;
Savitṛ-prasavi consists of ten, and here there is an increase by two in each case.
By Bṛhaspati, the Brahman priest, there were fifteen verses;
likewise by the two Aśvins, fifteen; the fifth [verse] was by Vṛc, thirteen by Kuvid-aṅga, and seven by Vṛc, four by Visruk.
"O you two, on the twelfth [day] one should bring the *surāman* and the *trivṛt* which has flowed forth;
on the seventeenth [day], like a son, one should bring from the two [sets] five and one"—
thus it is said in the *Padakārikāratnāvalī* on the *Vājasaneyisaṃhitā*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
The eleventh chapter is completed.
Now begins the twelfth chapter:
on the thirteenth day, one should perform the *yuñjāna* rite, and on the sixteenth day, the *vṛddhi* rite.
With the *yuktena* [verse], there are eight; the second is the single *ṛc*;
having joined (*yuktvāya*), on the fourteenth day, there are four; *visruto dvinān*, nine; with ten, two; the *ṛc* and the group of six.
For whom [the verse] "priyānavadaśastribhyaśca ṣaḍbhiḥ" is prescribed, O God Savitṛ; likewise, twenty [verses] with three [stomas], then eight;
he takes up the fifteen-fold [stoma] for two [verses], and one is desired for the Vṛkṣa.
You are the spade; on the fourteenth day, place one *vela* here with one hand; on the sixteenth day, let there be three, and again three;
then, being well-pleased, [place them] with eighteen, two for the second, and one.
The *yuñjāna* [hymn] has eight verses; the *arvāṅ* [hymn], two; the *navavṛt*, one; and the *anantaka* [hymn], none.
In the *yoge-yoge* [hymn], there are seventy-three; then, in the two [subsequent hymns], twenty-six; then, in the *pratūrti* [hymn], twenty; and finally, three in four [verses] respectively.

The *pṛthivyāḥ sadhasthāt* verses are ten; the first [verse] is with three [verses], as in the case of *yathānvagniḥ*, which consists of eighteen or three; and in the three [sections] there is one each.
Or, having approached on the thirteenth day, one should perform the second [rite] in two [days].
Having stepped upon the fifteenth day, likewise one, three, and one;
O you of many names, your back is on the fifteenth day with two and with four;
step forth on the sixteenth day with four, five, and one.
He stepped out with nineteen, or with six; they came with six;
he seized it at the *ṣoḍaśin* with one measure, and then with oneness;
from all sides with fifteen, and also with three and five.
And *parivājapatir vaḥ* once; *tṛtīyam* [is recited] at the third [veṣṭa]; *pari tvāgne puruvāra* on the twelfth, in three veṣṭas;
*tvam agne dyubhiḥ* on the thirteenth; and the three times seven are well-known.
There are twenty-two stations of the earth; four with four [verses each],
the surface of the waters as the seventeenth, the *visruk* as the end of the single [set] of five,
the *pañcadaśa* as the refuge, and one should bring forth four from the pair.
Dwell together; you are the twenty-first. With three, with six, I have kindled you.
O Agni, from the lotus-leaf, ten [singers] have brought you forth; three have found you.
To you, Dadhyañc, with ten and with three, the three have spoken.
*tamu* [is used] for the *apābhyaḥ*; *tvā* occurs ten times; *ca tvāyi* once; *ekam* once; *ekakam* once; *sīda* once; *ahodat* ten times; *navadaśa* nine times; *catvāri* four times;
*caturuṣu* four times; *dvayoḥ* twice; *ni hotā* once; and on the thirteenth [verse], *ṣaṭkam*, *aṣṭau*, and likewise *ekakam*.
On the fourteenth day, one [verse] for each of the two; likewise, one on the thirteenth day;
the "apo devīḥ" [verses] on the thirteenth day; four [verses] with six [stomas] for the taking of food; "saṃ te vāyuḥ" [is used] eighteen times; and one or three [verses] they ascended.
On the fourteenth day, *sujāta* consists of four; then, with three, there are [the verses] beginning with "ud u tiṣṭha," which are seventeen; of these four, however, there are three.
With the verse beginning "ūrdhva ū ṣu ṇaḥ," on the sixteenth day, there are four, and likewise six.

He was born as Gānavadaśa; with ten [syllables] each, he became two [groups], and with thirteen he became firm. Three and seven became one, and fourteen became Śiva. There is oneness in the two [groups of] five.
On the fourteenth day, let the Steed proceed; there are two emissions (visarga), likewise one and nine;
the Bull is nineteen, but Agni has one emission and one;
the plants are nineteen, four, and seven for two.
The thirteen *oṣadhi* verses, the three *vṛtra* verses, and the six [verses] he recites with power; with the sixteen, with the three, and again with the seven;
with the eleven *āpo hiṣṭhā* verses, and again one [verse] with five *vṛt* verses.
In the tenth month, Śiva is most auspicious; thereafter, in the seventh month, there is the dual [period];
therefore, in the eleventh month, it is likewise in three months;
Maitra occurs in the fourteenth month, and in the four [months], there is increase in two months of the *sruva*.

The fourteen Rudras, having been created as one, are distributed in sequence among the five; on the twelfth day they are created as two, and indeed by three [factors] there is the twelfth day; Sinīvālī is here said to be one by three.
One should fashion the *ukhā* as the seventeenth; two and one are mentioned together.
Having made forty-seven for Makha, fifteen and one, and having made thirteen from one, then one from two.
"Vasavas, you—twenty-three; here again with two [verses] by eight;
Aditi, you—with nine, and again with two for two [verses];
'Of the gods, you'—nineteen, with three, and again with nine."

*Mitrasya carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ*, *sapta vayaḥ*, and *tisṛbhir eva*; likewise, *devas tvā savitā* and *uśanā* with three and six verses respectively; for the *ukthya*, the twenty-one-fold [stoma] and one by one are praised.
On the seventeenth day, he offers Ākūti with six verses; on the fourteenth day, two [verses] of Dravasyati Māsubhitthā; there are four Visarjanā offerings;
with twenty verses, Dṛmhaskadevi; likewise, one [verse] for Visrug and one for Ekanān.
There are eight *dravaṇas* and *sarpiras*; from two and from eight;
from the one following [the eighth], on the twelfth, there may be one or two, making two;
and from the last, with three and with six, there are twelve.
O Agni, whatever [verses] there are consisting of seventeen feet, then from that;
on the fourteenth day, two are desired for the *vṛc* and one for the *iṣ*.
Day by day, there are seventeen, four, six, and likewise the *avisruk*.
The *nābhā-pṛṣṭhī* is the fifteenth; then there are four, and from that, two.
I shall go to the seventeenth on the two [verses]; from the seven, one for each.
With the two tusks, on the twelfth [day], with three [verses] two, and five.
Those among people who, on the thirteenth day, [offer] one, five, and one;
and who likewise offer to us seventeen, and one, and five, and one—
may they obtain four and two from my sharpened [sacrifice] on the thirteenth day.
On the fifteenth day of these [fortnights], there are two [offerings] and likewise one;
on the sixteenth day of the Lord of Food (Annapati), there are five; the fifth [offering] is for Visnu;
then the Ādityas with twenty, and then two in the sequence of nine.
Thus ends the twelfth chapter in the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
Now begins the thirteenth chapter.
The *Daśānī* has eighteen [verses], the *Rukma* eleven with three [additional verses], and likewise the *Naktoṣāsā* sixteen; the *Ṣaḍbhiḥ* has five, and the *Ekamena* one;
the *Viśvārūpāṇi* has twenty, and the three *Visrutāḥ* have four each.
With the ten verses beginning "suparṇo 'si," there are three triplets; the Stoma is the body with one [verse] on the fourteenth day; with two [verses], four are diffused;
"suparṇo 'si" consists of thirty-six, eight, nine, and one.
Agni cried out with twenty; four with seven;
for two [verses], fourteen; O Agni, come back! Two; one was chosen, not the last;
twenty-two, O Agni Aṅgiras; then two were chosen with seven.
Furthermore, *punarūrjā* consists of ten [verses]; among those, one is well-known as a single [verse].
From the seventeenth [chapter], I have taken one; and here, *vṛt* consists of six [verses].
*uduttamaḥ* consists of eighteen [verses], and here it is said that one [verse] consists of two [parts].
At the beginning, Bṛhat says ten; then two, seven, and two;
then you sit with twenty-one; then two, five, and one;
within the fire, on the fourteenth day, one, five, and likewise one.
Having become auspicious on the seventeenth day, one [verse] is applied with six [others] in due order;
on the seventeenth day after the day, four [are applied] with six; but here we know that among those thirty-one, one is employed across three [days].

In the eighteenth [verse], "samudre tvā," there are ten syllables; then, "pañcapañcadvayam" [is the next]; then follows "śrīṇām udāraḥ" with seventeen [syllables]; then four [syllables] for the seventeenth [verse];
likewise, "viśvasya ketuḥ" has eighteen [syllables]; and the unification of two [verses] occurs through four [syllables].
Uśik-pāvaka is eighteen; one and vṛt-pañcama are unity; those which you [possess] today are nineteen; there are four, and likewise two;
Ātam-bhajan is nineteen; he was defeated by two and by three.
"tvām agne" has eighteen [syllables]; "yajā" has one; "catubhir ekatā" is praised as Agni; "pañcadaśīm" belongs to seven and also to six;
and "ud ut tvā" occurs in the fifteenth [verse], with four [syllables] and again with seven.
O Agni, on the fifteenth day, there are four [verses]; then six and two;
"dvāviṃśati-prapṛccha" is one section; then the eighth [day] has eight;
"āpo devīḥ" with twenty [verses], and likewise four and four.
In the *apsu* [hymn], O Agni, there are twelve verses; with two [verses] there are four more;
with the twelfth verse, the four known as *garbho asi* are included;
and with the fourteenth verse, the three, four, and one are unified.
Furthermore, up to the fourteenth day, there are five renowned Vṛttis;
Bodha consists of eighteen, from two and five respectively;
and Sabodhisūri is held to consist of nine, three, two, and one.
Twenty-four minus one, and one with sixty is called the "name" (saṃjñāna); eighteen with five in the five in succession;
this is that Agni, nine and ten with two, and then five and three.
There are twenty-three verses for the Āgneyas; likewise, there are three and sixty.

For Agni, there are nineteen; for the two [worlds], nine; and likewise one. There are five for the Purīṣya Agnis, and ten for the two [sets of] Agnis. There are eight and twenty [verses] for the Vṛdhanvant [hymns].
O Agni, Ilā is the nineteenth; on the fifth day, there is likewise a fifth [brick].
You are indeed the fourteenth; and one *iṣṭaka* is for you.
On the two fourteenth days, there is one *lokapṛṇā* brick; likewise, one is formed by three [bricks] on each of the two [days].
Of these, on the thirteenth day, one [is prescribed]; five and one are desired; from Indra and Viśve [the deities], four [are taken] from ten; two are combined into one;
and on the eleventh day, four with a single binding.
"Saṃ vo manāṃsi," "Viṃśatyā," "Tatra dvayadvayoḥ," then "Pañcadaśyā," "Agnitvaṃ pari," "Dvayośca pañcamīdvayam," "Mātā iva putrān aṣṭādaśaḥ," and "Pañca vṛt ṣaḍbhiḥ."
*asunvantam*—nineteen and one; *vṛddham*—two; *eva ca*—one; *namassute*—nineteen; *catvāri*—four; *tritayam*—three; *tataḥ*—then;
*yasyāste ghore*—twenty; *tribhiḥ*—three; *pañca*—five; *ekam eva ca*—and one.
The goddess has twenty-five parts; the fourth consists of four, while the fifth becomes the dwelling-place.
The sixteenth part indeed has five functions, and with five they yoke the plough;
with ten they yoke one, and there are two for release.
From *yunakta sīrā* comes the twenty-second; then one with five verses;
*śunaṃ naḥ* has eighteen verses; then two [hymns] beginning with the fifth verse of *vṛt*;
then *ghṛtena sītā* has eighteen verses; then two [hymns] consisting of three verses each and one [verse].
On the fourteenth day, the plow (lāṅgala) is joined with five wrappings;
on the eleventh day, the wish-fulfilling cow (kāmadugha) with three; on the two [preceding days], the vṛsruk is released with ten; and there is one [day] with four flowing [streams].
Fourteen together with the year, four indeed with ten,
those herbs which are fifteen, and one with five;
or a hundred on the fifteenth day— therein, one becomes four.
With nine [verses] for the herbs, again with four and seven;
"The ten herbs" is one, and the fifth is the *vṛt*;
on the fourteenth day, with three and indeed with four, like the *aśvattha*.
The *Oṣadhī* hymn is on the eleventh day; here, four [verses] are recited with six [stomas].
However, the *Daśāśvavatī* or the *Soma* hymn is desired as two sets of four.
On the *Ucchunī* day, there is one *Oṣadhī* hymn on the eleventh day; then, two [hymns] are performed with two [stomas], and likewise in the subsequent [day].
The fifteenth [verse] is named *pañcadaśoṣkṛti*;
it consists of two [padas] among five *visruṣ* (streams), exceeding all others in the fourteenth;
here, however, there are thirteen [syllables], and if one measures them, they are two, three, and one.
On the eleventh [day], there are four medicinal herbs; likewise on the sixth, [one recites] "sākaṃ yakṣma prapatatu. On the twelfth, there is a single binding;
[one recites] "anyā vo anyām" and the sixteenth [verse]; likewise, with six [verses], there is the *visruk*.
May those that bear fruit, those twelve, and the one renowned as the aged,
release me on the eleventh day; there were three enclosures,
and on the thirteenth day, the two excellent ones here with five [leaves] pass away.
Those herbs which are established upon the earth on the thirteenth day— eight from three, five from five, two from two, and two thereafter;
and those which are here in the fifteen [days], three in the five streams.
On the eleventh day, there is one [deity] who is the destroyer; on two [days], three [deities] are the *visruks*;
on the fifteenth, two are the *veṣṭanas* and three are the *visruks*.
On the twelfth, the plants (*oṣadhayaḥ*) are two *visruks*, and at the end, there is one.
The Gandharvas [recite] for you on the fourteenth day: four, two, and fourteen; you are the highest among two, and one among five;
twenty-two; do not harm me; one, and indeed with seven.

The *abhyāvartasva* occurs on the twelfth day; then there are two *visargas*. "O Agni, that which is yours" occurs on the eleventh day. If one knows the *ekaviṃśati-sruk*, it is said that there is food (*iṣ*), strength (*ūrj*), nineteen [verses], and one *visarga*.
O Agni, your five [verses] with two and three [syllables],
O Visruk, O Pavaka, on the fourteenth [day], four and one on the sixth; and on the fourteenth, from the seven [verses] beginning with Ūrjānapāt, ten are renowned.
On the fifteenth day, while ruling, [he offers] two, four, and one;
on the fourteenth day, two, and again two;
on the fifteenth day, the observer of the seasons, four, and then three.

On the eleventh day, perform the *āpyāyasva* rite; here, however, there is one *vṛt* and one [verse]. There are seventeen *santepaya* verses; four are fifteen-fold, and eleven are *āpyāyasva*; with three [verses], there are five, ending with one.
May the eleven [verses] beginning with *ā te vatsa* and the two pairs [beginning with] *dvayaṃ dvitayam eva ca* be for you;

may the four renowned [verses] beginning with *tubhyam tāṃ giraḥ* [be for you]; and may the three renowned [verses] beginning with *agniḥ prayeṣu* [be for you], along with the ten [verses] beginning with *daśasu* and the two [beginning with] *dvābhyām*.
Thus ends the thirteenth chapter in the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the *Vājasaneyisaṃhitā*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
Now begins the fourteenth chapter.
On the twelfth day, I accept [the offerings] with three repetitions and three dismissals;
likewise on the fifth and eleventh days with the *brahmajajña* hymn of twenty-one verses,
and on the tenth with the *hiraṇyagarbha* hymn, as well as one with five verses.
Draṣṭṛ, Skandaikaviṃśa, and likewise Eka and Catasruka—homage be to them with fifteen [verses]; and all the others with five;
likewise those arrows on the fourteenth day—one, five, and one.
Thus, in the *evā mīḍhuṣe* hymn there are sixteen verses; in the *trayaṃ pañca* hymn there are five;
in the *visrutāḥ* hymn there are eighteen; in the *kṛṇuṣva pājaḥ* hymn there are four;
in the *caturaikatā* hymn there are four; in the *tabhūmā* hymn there are seventeen; and in the *dvābhyām* hymn there are four and one.
The *pratispaś* [verse] consists of twenty-two; the two [verses] beginning with "vṛddha" and "dvādaśī" [make twenty-four];
"visrug udagne tiṣṭha" is twenty-one; the two "velau" [make twenty-three]; the pair [of verses] is twenty-one;
"ūrdhvo bhava" is nineteen and one [making twenty]; and the two "vṛddha" [verses] are twenty-one.
"O Agni, I settle you with your brilliance; there are eight *visruk*s, one for each.
The sacrifice is seventeenfold; with three [verses] there are five *visarjanas*.
You are firm (*dhruvā*) on the fifteenth day; and with three [verses], there are two *visruk*s."
Prajāpati [is assigned] to you on the twelfth day, one for each;
likewise, Bhūrbhūmi on the fourteenth day, one; and Vṛt in the five [days] in sequence, one.
For the sake of all, by means of the twenty vital breaths, the five-fold one is desired as the single [deity].
From section to section: the twelfth, three, and again three in sequence;
that which is on the twelfth by a hundred, one for each of two, and indeed one alone;
those of yours, O Agni, in the sun, on the sixteenth, and in the seven streams of the two.
The sixteenth [verse] consists of "yā devāśca" and "vṛdekaṃ tu"; "bhavā visruk" and "virāḍ jyotiḥ" constitute the twelfth; "tribhiścatvāri" and "visrutāḥ" are [the next];
"viśvasmai" consists of fifteen [syllables], and here there are three for each of the three [sections].
Madhu [is on] the thirty-seventh; Vṛddhi [is on] the twelfth and the thirteenth;
Aṣṭāhlāsin [is on] the twelfth; likewise, Dvaya and Dvitaya together with Sva [are on] the eleventh; and also [the others] with three for each of the two.
The *madhu* wind blows in ten directions, and likewise one in the fifth; the *madhunakta* wind blows in twelve, and likewise one in the fourth;
the *apāṅga* asterism is in the nineteenth, and one [wind] from three and seven.
Three, eighteen, three, five, and likewise three;
nine, ten, five, six, and then one; for the sake of food and wealth, there are sixteen, two enclosures, and likewise also [one].
O Agni, on the eleventh day, you yoke [the drops] at two discharges; then on the twelfth, O God, you yoke them at ten; likewise, on the thirteenth, you flow perfectly for three, then for two;
on the seventeenth, eight are poured forth.
"Ṛce tvā," "Ruce tvā," "Abhāse," the fourteenth [verse], the eleven-fold [hymn], "Agni with light," the ten [verses], the single occurrence, then two [verses],
the seventeenth [verse], "Āditya," "Garbham," "Trasaḥ," "Vṛccha," then two [verses].
For Vāta, on the seventeenth [verse], there are two, one, and one;
the seventeen-fold Indu continuously for five [verses], and from the fifth, the *sukra*;
"Varūtrī" as the seventeenth, one [verse], and one with the *vṛti*s.
The fire that is Agni, which is twenty-onefold, the two, the seven, and the thirty-two—
do not harm this one; and the two among the five,
the single-hoofed, the ten, the one, the thousandfold, the elevenfold, and the twentyfold.

On the twelfth day, [the hymns] beginning with "varuṇasya" consist of three; on the two [following days], there are two; [then] "ajo hy agne" with twenty-one verses; "visruk" with five; and "ca nān" with two.
On the eleventh day, however, "tvaṃ yaviṣṭha" consists of eleven; then there are two *visargas*, and finally one *nān*.
There are twenty-six [verses] for the waters; these [are] three times nine, ending with the *vinnā* verses, likewise three, ten, this [one] for the *purobhū*s, two, and six;
for the *gāyatrī*, the fifteenth [verse] is for the cows, and the seventh here is with six.
This [verse] from the south consists of ten syllables; then three times three [syllables] form three *vṛtis*. Then there are fifteen *triṣṭubh* syllables, followed again by eight and nine.
This [verse] from the west consists of ten syllables, while we [the others] become four.
From the *jagatī* there are fifteen; from the *saptavṛt* seven, and from the *saptaviśrutā* ten;
likewise from the *uttarā* ten, and from two *vṛt*s one each;
from the *anuṣṭubh*s fifteen, and from the *pañcavṛt*s six indeed.

"Daśeyamuparimiti" is the *visruk*; "catvāra eva ca paṅktibhiḥ" is the *nidhana*; "ekaviṃśaścāṣṭau vṛt ṣaṭca visrutāḥ"—thus [ends] the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the Vājasaneyisaṃhitā composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
The fourteenth chapter;
now the fifteenth chapter:
eighteen, nine, four, and two.
In the sixteenth [chapter], however, there are four [cities] for the two [groups] in the fourth [section] by means of their own eighteen dexterous [verses]; and for the two elders,
the city of the Earth is renowned as twenty-four, and the four are likewise celebrated.
May Aditi protect me with twenty-one; may the three renowned ones with six;
may Sajūs on the fourteenth day with five; likewise may Dvādaśa;
and may Prāṇa with thirteen, two, and one, grant me knowledge.
The *Apaḥ pinvat* has twelve verses; the next two have four each;
the *Mūrdhā* has ten; the fifth has four;
the *Vistra* has eight; and the *Basta* likewise has four.
The *sim̐hadī* has eight or sixteen *velās*, or four;
the *anaḍvān* is said to have eight, four, three, or one;
the *pañcāvī* consists of five *gāyatrīs*; and seven, four, and three are thus declared.
"O Indra and Agni, [protect] the undeviating Ekādaśī and Vṛddhi;
Viśvakarman shall be the Ṣaṣṭhī; there is one Vṛcchaikaviṃśa and the Pañcavṛccha; may you become four."
My life-span is seventeen; four are renowned in two [verses];
Mācchanda and Pramā are said to be seven and two; three Vṛttas are proclaimed;
the Bṛhatī and Anuṣṭubh should be a group of six; and there are three Veṣṭanas at the beginning.
From the earth to the intermediate space, there are six; likewise, from the emission (visarga), there are two.
Mind and agriculture [arise] from seven; but from the fifth, Visruj and Gavai [arise]. In the fifteenth, Agni is the deity; likewise, the emissions are twelve.
The head-vein (*mūrdhāsirāṭ*) is on the eleventh; the *yantrīradya* is the thirteenth;
the swift (*āśu*) is the twenty-three-fold;
the embryos (*garbhāḥ*) are the seventeen-fold; and the tenfold and sixteenfold [stomas] are likewise.
The eighteenth [verse] belongs to Agni; the eighth consists of four *vṛt* verses;
the eleventh consists of twenty-five *vṛt* verses for the Nṛcakṣases;
the fifth consists of eighteen [verses] for the Vasus; and there are ten well-known [verses].
The Aditi [hymn] consists of twenty verses; likewise, the Vṛdhanmatī is the fifteenth [of the Vālakhilyas].
With twenty-three [verses], the Yava [hymn] has six [sections]; the Viśruk has twelve;
and with one [verse], there are thirty; and with ten, thirteen.
By nine [there are] twenty-eight; by eight, eight; by fourteen, seventeen; by one, thirty-one; by ten, fourteen;
likewise by twenty-five, forty-six; and by fifteen, eleven.
The Visargas are eighteen, and there are four in the name-mantra;
thus ends the fifteenth chapter in the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the Vājasaneyi-Saṃhitā, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
Now begins the sixteenth chapter:
twenty, four hundred and five, five, one thousand,
twenty-eight, five, eleven, and four in the [first] four [sections].

The *purīṣa* of Agni consists of twenty; there are four *vṛtti*s, and *visruk* is indeed the metre. *Varivas* consists of eight; there are three *vṛt*s. With seven [syllables], *visruk* is the Sindhu and the Samudra in the seventh [verse]; and in two [verses], there is one *visruk*.
The sequence of syllables consists of nine, seven, five, and eight;
the Bṛhat and Rathantara [Sāmans] consist of five and four [syllables] respectively;
and on the eleventh [verse], five, six, and eight [syllables] are proclaimed.
With *raśmi*, *satyāyasatya* [is formed]; with *tari* and *visruk*, the thirteenth;
and with *pratidhi*, the twelfth. Three [syllables] are elided here, but one remains.
With *uśijā*, *vasu* [is formed] on the fourteenth; three [syllables] and four [syllables] are elided in two [cases].
The medicinal herbs are [placed] on the thirteenth [spoke]; this is called the "five-six-six group.
From the tenth [spoke] onwards, there is the *pratipad* (first lunar day) group; in the six [spokes], the *vṛt* (turn) group consists of twenty-one *srug*s.
For the three *trivṛt*s, there are eight *veṣṭana*s (wrappings) in the sixth [spoke], respectively.
In this manner, there is the *ākrama* and the *ṣoḍaśī*; likewise, the ten-fold, the five-fold, and the *visruta*.
O Queen, on the eleventh day of the waxing moon, there are four for two [days];
through the three-fold state, on the thirteenth day, there is the three-fold and the one-fold *visruta*.
The twenty-four sages [honored] you on the fifth; the six renowned ones on the sixth; on the eleventh of the Virāj, the three and the four;
on the thirteenth, the fifteen; and on the two [days], the two who have increased and are renowned.
One should perform the *samrāṭ* on the eleventh day, as well as the *trayovṛt* and the *catura*;
the *saptadaśa-stoma*, however, belongs to the thirteenth day. There are two [stomas] for each of the two [days];
on the eleventh day there is the *svarāla*, and four are renowned as being with three [verses].

Then, on the eleventh day, one should perform the *vṛt* [chanting] three times for the three [stomas], and for the sake of sovereignty (*adhipatnye*), one should perform it with three [verses] in three [stomas] in succession;
then on the thirteenth day, one should perform the *vṛt* six times for the twenty-seven and thirty-three [stomas].
This [verse] and the next consist of twenty-one and eight syllables respectively; then there is one of eleven syllables.
To them, salutation! Then there is one of twenty syllables with a *visarga*, and after that, this thirteenth [verse] has six syllables, with five [syllables] flowing forth.
This [constellation] is behind on the thirteenth day, renowned for six, seven, and twenty-three;
this [constellation] is above on the thirteenth day, renowned for three;
this [constellation] is above on the thirteenth day, ending with seven, five, and one.
The wise know that this Agni has nine emissions;
Agni was awakened on the seventeenth [day] with six [verses], and four [verses] were emitted;
"on the fifteenth we have spoken," so they say, and two [verses] were emitted by means of two.

The *Janasya gopāḥ* [is recited] on the sixteenth day; four [verses] on the seventeenth; twenty-one [verses] on the eighteenth; nineteen [verses] on the nineteenth; one [verse] on the twentieth; seven [verses] on the twenty-first;
one [verse] on the twenty-second; and thirteen [verses] on the twenty-third, with three concluding *visarjana* rites.
With the seventeenth [verse], "sam̐ samidhye," there is one [verse] by Caturaka;

with the thirteenth, "tvām agne haviṣmantaḥ," there are eleven [verses] by Ekavr̥ti; with the [verse] "tvāṃ citraśravaḥ," there are ten; thus the three [collections] are distributed among the three [sections].
The *enāva*, *agni*, and the fifteen-versed hymn are said to be one group;
the *viśva* is the swift one among thirteen, while the third belongs to two;
the *samudra* is with ten, and three are renowned as fourfold.
"O Agni, [recite] one verse on the eleventh day; then four verses with five [verses each]; then on the eleventh day, kindling [the fire], one more; then on the sixth day, one;
O King, on the thirteenth day, one, then five, and likewise one."
May Agni be auspicious to us on the twelfth; on the thirteenth, may they be renowned for their triple-fold strength;

on the fourteenth, may there be four auspicious ones; on the fifteenth, four [verses] with four *visrūks*; on the eleventh, [a hymn] with which one wins in battle; and on the third and second [days], likewise.
I consider that fire to be nine, ten, and eight;
that fire is one, nine, and ten; four, ten, and seventeen respectively; both are well-shining, five-layered, and five-fold in their outpourings.
On the thirteenth day, one should choose one [verse] for Agni; if there are two, then on the eleventh day for Agni, let there be four *visargas*.
With these *narks*, one should choose one on the thirteenth day, and then nine.

The twenty-fourth [verse] is addressed to Agni; the Hotṛ [priest] [recites] for five [verses] in the four-fifths [sections]; those who are the sages are nineteen; in the sixth [section], there are two ending with six;
that [section] has nineteen with the wives; in two [sections], there are seventeen renowned ones.
On the seventeenth day, or again on the third and the ninth;
this Agni is the fifteenth, while four are the sixteenth and the seventeenth; having moved from the fifteenth, there is then the single [day].
Twenty; "Awake, O Agni" (three verses); two [verses] by means of two;
then two; the fourteenth; one verse for Enava-ha; likewise two for Vṛc;
"Tapaḥ-tapasya" (six verses); one verse for Padāś-eka; and four for Bhavan.
Twenty-two, *prothadaśva*, and one; *vṛc* [is used] four times and once;
*āyoṣṭvāsadane viṃśat* [is used] once; *vṛc* twice; *visruk* [is used] eight times; and for *sahasrasya-pramā*, three *vṛc*s and one [are] desired.
Thus ends the sixteenth chapter in the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the *Vājasaneyisaṃhitā*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
Now begins the seventeenth chapter.
Salutations to you, O Rudra! On the twelfth day, one should recite "dvau vṛca" and also "tribhiḥ";
on the fourteenth day, "yāte rudra," one should recite "trayo vṛca" and "dvayor visruk.
In the "yāmiṣu" hymn, on the fourteenth day, one should recite "dvayaṃ vṛca" and "ekam eva ca."
He protected with auspicious speech; he spoke fourteen [verses] for two [days], two for each;
the *Ṣoḷaśīya* chant was the second; three [days] had five [verses];
that Tāmravarṇa had nineteen; and ten [verses] were renowned as being for two [days].
He who [is present] on the fourteenth and the fifteenth, and likewise eight and two upon you;
salutations to him who is on the thirteenth, becoming four for three [days]; he releases one on the sixteenth, and likewise seven on the seventh.
On the thirteenth day, the bow is to be worshipped; four [arrows] with seven [feathers], two on the sixteenth, two bows, and one on the fourteenth;
when the fifteenth day has passed, one [arrow] with four [feathers] becomes one.

Having bent the twelve-finger bow, from five [arrows] four [hit the mark]; salutations to you! On the twelfth day, one was struck; if on two days, it was great pride. And on the twenty-seventh, one was struck; ten were renowned.
On the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight, there is one [offering] and four trees for each; on the sixteenth day, there are sixteen [offerings] and likewise four trees for six;
and on the twelfth day for Babhruśāya, there are two wrappings.
For Rohitāya on the twelfth day, there are three [vessels], and then two for Apivāt;
