for Kṛtsnāvītāya, the twelve [vessels] are wrapped in a sequence of five. But for Vañcate on the thirteenth day, there are four [vessels] with seven [wrappings].
To the one with the turban (*uṣṇīṣin*), the eleventh; the seventh of the seven dancers (*saptanṛt*);
*visruk*, he who emits; eight [verses] for the *vidyā*; of the six, the eighth of the trees (*vṛkṣa*);
*visruk*, from the assemblies (*sabhā*) for the lord of the assembly (*sabhāpati*); eight [verses] for the four, and the eighth is *visruk*.
If the eighth [verse] belongs to the Gaṇas, or if the eighth belongs to the five, or if the eight [verses] belong to the Senās on the twelfth day, or if the fifth and the eighth belong to the Visras;
for the Takṣas, there should be the fifth and again the eighth.
For the dogs, one should perform eight [offerings] for the Lord of Dogs; then two sets of five for the Kapardin;
with eight [verses], one should perform seven [offerings] for the Ekavisruta;
for the Hrasva, there should be eight [offerings] and one verse; for the Āśu, there should be eight [offerings] and one verse.
For Jyeṣṭhā, there should be eight [syllables] with three *vṛt*s; for Sobhyā, two sets of eight with *vṛt*; for Niyā, eight with four *vṛt*s; for Bilminī, there should be two sets of eight;
for Dhṛṣṇu, eight with five *vṛt*s; and for Srutī, there should be eight *pada*s.
In the case of the *kūpyā* [section], there should be an increase of eight; from the *vātyā* [section] onwards, there is an increase of one for each.
For the *śaṅku* [section], there is an increase of four; for the tree [section], nine and six;
for the three [sections], eight and two; and for the *sikatī* [section], there should be an increase of eight and two.
The *vrajajyāṣṭavṛt* [is used] for the *śuṣkyā*, the *aṣṭaikaveṣṭana* for the *parṇyā*; the *ṣoḍaśī* for the *daśavṛt*, and the *navavisruta* for the *drā*.
The *navadaśī* is used for the *indhas*, and the four [verses] for the three *visrus*.

These Rudras are eighteen; in the three modes of activity there is oneness, and they reach the fifteenth Rudra; then the two emissions (visargas) follow, and thereafter there are eighteen for us, as well as the pair and the group of six.
Mīḍhuṣṭama [is praised] with eight [verses]; the eighteenth [hymn] consists of four; five are well-known;
five for the tenth [verse], Vikiriṇa for three; with five [verses] for Vṛc [in the eleventh];
and eleven thousand [are the total] here for two, with five [for each].
The Ekādaśī is uncounted; the Visrug of the two increases is one;
in this great [system], of the six there is one Visrug; likewise, from the one, the Nīlagrīvā is fivefold; and the Trivṛt is fourfold with three Visrugs.

Śarva [is worshipped] three times below, three times on the forehead, and four times on the two eyes; Bhūta [is worshipped] three times on the two arms and four times on the two shoulders; Pathin [is worshipped] four times on the four limbs and twice on the two knees; Tīrtha [is worshipped] four times on the four sides and twice on the two feet; and likewise, the fifth [deity] is worshipped five times on the five parts of the body.

One *vṛddha* with one *visarga*, one ending in *n*, one ending in *m*, one with seven vowels, one with four *visargas*, and one with nine *visargas* in sequence—these are praised as the nine [names]. *Namaḥ* has nine *visargas*. *Turu* has ten. *Navadaśī* (the ninth) has nine *visargas*. *Vṛt* has four *visargas*. *Visrug* has one. And one ending in *n* is recommended. These are the seven. And one ending in *m* and one with seven vowels. *Vṛt* has four *visargas*. *Visrug* has one. *Namaḥ* has nine *visargas*. *Turu* has ten. *Navadaśī* has nine *visargas* in sequence.
Thus ends the seventeenth chapter in the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya;
now begins the eighteenth chapter.
The *Navaviṃśati*, *Aśman*, and *Ūrja* [are recited] four times; the eighth is for two [verses].
*Imā me agne* is on the thirteenth day, and one [verse] is for three [recitations].
The fifteenth is *Arbuda*, and likewise one [verse] is for six [recitations].
The Ṛtavaḥ consists of twelve syllables, while the Saptabhiḥ consists of nine;
two exhalations (visrugs) of the ocean are proclaimed as having ten syllables each. The Jarā of Himā consists of ten syllables; thus, there are two exhalations here.
Twenty-three on the day of stepping forth; one, two, and likewise one;
the milk-oblation on the fourteenth; two with three for the soma-pressing;
O Agni Pāvaka, eleven on the eleventh; and one at the very end here.
*Sanaḥ pāvaka* on the fourteenth [tithi] consists of one, five, and one;
in *pāvake* with twenty-one [syllables], *visruk* consists of five, three, and nine;
and *namaste* consists of twenty-four, five, six, and one.
On the seventeenth day, those deities who are one become unified with five;
those deities who are twenty-four are said to be seven in two;
on the fourteenth day, the givers of breath and the fifteen-fold ones become one.
On the eleventh day, *agni* (fire) with its sharp edge (*tigmena*) is mentioned; three emissions (*visarga*) are proclaimed.
On the nineteenth day, however, there are these [syllables]: the fifth and the unity of the two increases (*vṛddhi*).
What indeed was the eighteenth? Of the four, there are two and one.
The fifteenth, the all-seeing with six;

the ten and the one in the twenty-first; what indeed is the forest with five and seven; the single one with nine and eighteen; those stations of yours which are threefold, thrice-three, and once manifold.
The father of the eye is eighteen; three are spread across the three [worlds];
Viśvakarman is nineteen; in the sixth [section] there are four and one;
the father is twenty; and here, however, there are three, six, and eight.
He who perceives the ninefold path with two, and likewise with two and one;
beyond that, twenty; therein, one; seven are the flowing streams;
him as the embryo of nineteen; one in three, and one alone.
On the seventeenth [verse], there is *nataṃ vidātha* with two [verses] and four *visrutāḥ*;
on the eighteenth, the *viśvakarmāṇi* with two and four;
on the sixteenth, *āśuḥ śiśānaḥ*; and from three, the eleven *avisruk*.
Saṃkrandana [is assigned] to the fifteenth [tithi] with five [arrows]; Visruk, with arrows in hand, [is assigned] to the three [tithis] following the sixteenth; Aṣṭa becomes the ninth;
Bṛhaspati [is assigned] to the fourteenth with four [arrows], and Traya to the four [tithis] following that.
In the sixteenth [moment], one who possesses power and discernment [attains] six; in the eighth, one [attains] one.
But in the sixteenth, one who breaks through the lineage [attains] five; and in the two [moments], only two.
In the sixteenth, those with the lineage of non-attainment [attain] three; in the three [moments], nine are renowned as increasing.
Indra [took] the fifteenth of these; Vr̥tra [took] two; six flowed away.
From the fifteenth of the bull Indra, the seers extracted four verses from two [verses], then the seventeenth from two, and one from two.
O Indra, eighteen belong to us;
likewise, three of the six and nineteen of these others; two have pierced the mind of three, and the fifteenth has been released as two, one, and one.
On the fifteenth day, O Preta, there were victories and twenty-seven dismissals;
that army which was twenty-one [strong] became two, and by three they became one,
where the arrows were fifteen, and from the two, seven were scattered abroad.
Your vital points (*marmāṇi*) are twenty; the emissions (*visargāḥ*) are five. Being the fifth, it arises with *uden*. The fifteenth, however, is the triple-vṛt and single-ucyuta;
in Indra, it is called the fourteenth, the triple-vṛt and single-ucyuta, which is to be meditated upon (*mantu*).
For whomsoever there is the *ṣoḍaśī* [stotra], let the five-fold [oblation] proceed;
in the three and three [verses], and in the eight, they are well-spread;
in the *ṣoḍaśī*, when the fire is kindled, there are four in the five [verses] in succession.
On this fourteenth day of the gods, there are four, eight, and likewise one; on the fifteenth day, the oblation is offered to Vīta, one, and seven;
to Saptadaśī, Sūrya, Raśmi, four, and three in the four.

On the thirteenth [syllable], there are five, three, and two;
then on the fourteenth, the *udgrāha* consists of four and one, followed by three in succession.
On the thirteenth, however, you should step forward; the fifth is the *visarga*.
The *Prācīmatī* is said to have twenty-one [verses], four, eight, and one;
the *Pṛthivī* has seventeen, and its four [sections] are well-known;
the *Svaryantī* has fourteen, and its four [sections] consist of four [verses] each.
O Agni, with sixteen [verses] for the *prehi* [section], recite three [times] with seven [verses] each;
O Agni, with seventeen [verses], recite three thousand [times] with three [verses] each, and then one by one;
with "suparṇo 'si" [and] eighteen [verses], recite one; with "vṛtrāya" [and] one [verse], recite one.
With nine verses, the third [section] is recited; "vṛddhayaṃ visruk" [is the first], then eighteen for Savitṛ, four, and two are stated.
With nineteen verses, four, two, and one are likewise recited.
Taking [the oblation], O Agni, on the thirteenth day, I offer the single-fold, the five-fold, and the renowned; the eighteen-fold, the four-fold, the five-fold, and the one-fold;
twenty-two, seven, and that one-fold, O Agni, again with fivefold layers.
Śukrajyotis with eight, or five, six, and likewise one;
Īdṛṅ and Saptavadhri with seven, four, and three;
Ṛtajit and Satyajit with seven, six, and four, celebrated [as such].
In the *Ṛtasatya*, there are seven fixed [verses]; in two [sections], there are seven well-known [verses] increased by five;
such are the seventeen [verses], with five increased by one, [forming] the *Svatavān* and *Praghāsin* [sections], which consist of seven, five, and one [respectively].
"Indra," "na," "daivī," "trayoviṃśatiḥ," "tribhyaḥ," "trayodaśīm," "dvayam"—
thus ends the eighteenth chapter in the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, composed by Śaṅkarācārya.

Now begins the nineteenth chapter: this [hymn] beginning with "imam" has seventeen verses; it consists of two *ṛc*s ending in "eka," followed by "ghṛtam mimikṣe," nineteen [syllables], and is characterized by the *trivṛt* meter, the number three, the number two, and the word "visruk."
The ocean [is] the tree; the nineteenth [verse] belongs to two [stomas], the twenty-first to one;
the seventeen-fold [stoma] is called *vaya*; it belongs to two [stomas], five and one, and four horns; the nineteenth [verse] belongs to two, seven, and one.
Three times nine, ten, and one; six, and then one;
these [verses] for Aruṣa; three, twenty-three, and likewise from three and nine;
like the fifteen [verses] of the ocean; four, and then one.
The *abhiplava* with the fifteen-fold [stoma], the three, and the eight *visarjanas*; "kaṃ ca" and "iva ca," the eighteen-fold, the two, the *vṛt*, the five, and the *visrutās*;
"mā abhya ṛṣata," the eighteen-fold, and then two by two.
The mantras consist of twenty-one, four, four, one, and nine; eighteen, four, and twelve are the *visruk*;
the out-breath (*prāṇa*) and the in-breath (*apāna*) are the twelfth, while three and six are the *visrutāḥ*.
Ojas was born on the twelfth day, while Visargas were four;
Jyeṣṭhya arose from my fourteenth [day], Vṛtra alone as the fifth,
Satya on the twelfth, Śraddhā likewise, and Yaṃ as the tenth.
The *pitṛn* [verse] should consist of twelve syllables; likewise for three and four [syllables].
The *yantāyantā* [verse] consists of two [padas]; with six [syllables], there is *śarmayaḥ priyam*; and with twelve and eight [syllables] as well.
The *ūrka* and the *nṛtā* are the twelfth; here, by two [syllables], there is also the *ṣaḷati* in the twelfth;
the *amṛta* is fourfold; in the two increases, the *visṛk* is the twelfth;
by the *caras*, the *āyas* is from three; and by three, the *vṛt* is as follows.
The *vīhayaḥ* (grains) and *yava* (barley) are twelve; likewise, the *visarga*s (emissions) are twelve;
the twelfth is *aśman* (stone), and the fifth is *nṛttikā* (clay), which are the *avisarjana*s (non-emissions).
On the thirteenth day are the waters of Agni; likewise, there are two sets of eleven.
The *vasu* and the dwelling (*vasati*) consist of eight [syllables] or five *visargas*;
Agni, Indra, and Soma consist of seven and four *visargas* respectively;
Mitra and Varuṇa as the seventh consist of four *visargas*.
The earth, the intermediate space, the seven, the four, the *visruk*;
the *aṃśu*, the *raśmi*, and the twelfth; the four, the twelve, the *visruk*;
the *āgrayaṇa* for the All-Gods (*vaiśvadeva*) with the twelve, and the thirteen with five.
The *sruva* and *ścamasa* [are mentioned] in the twelfth [chapter], with six and nine [verses] respectively; the *agni-gharma* is in the thirteenth; the *nisruk* has twelve increased by one;
the *vrata* and *mṛtavas* are declared to be three each, increased by two.
One, three, seventeen, eleven, nine, four, eight, and twelve;
five-fold, six, and those with two or three openings;
likewise, three and two in ten, and eight in three—these are the openings.
The *paṣṭhavāt* is twelve; one [verse] with three [syllables], one with nine and ten, [the verse] for the *svāhākāra*, seven, and one—this is the eighteen-fold [section];
with fourteen, two, and one [verse].
"Āyuḥ, yajñe, na, ṣoḷaśyām, visargaḥ; the seventh [verse] again has the *stoma* as *yajus*, the seventeenth [verse] has three turns (*trayovṛt*), and seven exits (*saptavisrugaḥ*)"—
thus [ends] the *Padakārikā Ratnamālā* composed by the venerable Śāṅkarācārya on the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā.
The nineteenth chapter is completed.
Now begins the twentieth chapter:
Viśve consists of twenty-one syllables, and for the two [next], there are six syllables each.
On the fourteenth day, Vāja belongs to three [gods] with nine [verses];
again, Vāja belongs to three [gods] with eighteen;
then Vāja belongs to two [gods] with eight, and one [verse] for each.
Release me into the fifteenfold, the single-streamed, and likewise the fourfold;
the milk, the earth, and the twenty-onefold; here, the tenfold, the *avisruk*, the *ṛtāṣāt*, the twentyfold, and likewise the one and the eightfold-streamed.

The *saṃhita* [is formed] with all nine [syllables]; there are six *visarjanas* in two [sections], and on the ninth [verse] is *Suṣumna*. In the sixth [section] of both [the *sūrya* and *vāyu* hymns], however, there are nine; *Iṣira*, *Viśvavyacas*, and one [more] in the seventh [section] are the *visrugas*.
Bhujyu Suparṇa with nine and one; as on the seventh [day], Navaprajāprati; Viśvakarman on the fourth; Sanaka in five;
Cāndravada with ten and one; and with three dismissals.
Fifteen, the ocean (four), three, and then two eights; then "rucaṃ naḥ" (fifteen), but then one, two, and twenty-four;
two, six, and eight—thus they are proclaimed.
The ninth [verse] is *sannava*; likewise, with six *caṣṭaḍ* and visarjanīya syllables, the seventeenth is "I yoke the fire" (*agniṃ yunajmi*). Three are *vṛcca*, two are *visruk*.
These are the nineteen; four are *vṛcca*, and the fifth is five.
Indu-dakṣa has eighteen; Diṣo-mūrdhā has four, ten, and one on the thirteenth [day], and two with six on the two [subsequent days];
Viśvasya-mūrdhā has twenty-two, as well as two, seven, and one.

The sacrifice was performed on the thirteenth day; Agni was worshipped in three, seven, eleven, and two [verses] respectively across the seven streams. From the intention [of the rite], there are twenty [verses], consisting of seven-fold and seven-streamed [hymns].
This [is] the eighteenth with six verses; the seventeenth with three, this one with one, and this one, O Lord, with five;
with one [verse] on the *prastara* grass-bundle, with fourteen [verses], and with two [verses] on the two [fires].
That which was given, and indeed that which was offered,
where there were fourteen streams by means of two bowstrings and eight [arrows], and likewise two fires in the fourteenth [night], they became four.
The Vārtrahatya [hymn] consists of eight verses; following that are two *veṣṭa* sections.
Then comes the *sahadānu*, which is the *ṣoḍaśin*; here, however, there are two *veṣṭa* sections.
The *mṛga-nabhīma* consists of twenty verses, followed by three and seven [verses], and then the *ekanān*.
Vaiśvānara [is the first]; on the eleventh day, the second is the Vṛṣala; then, the Pṛṣṭha [stotras] are twenty-one; the Visargas are thirteen;
the Abhyātāna is the nineteenth; and there are two of the second kind.

"We [chant] the *vayaṃ te* [hymn] with seventeen verses; two [verses] for the second [day], one for the *dhāma*, and on the fourteenth [day] with two [verses]; the *vṛt* and *saptaviṣrugāḥ* [are chanted] with two [verses].
Thus, in the *Padakārikāratnamālā* composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya, within the *Vājasaneyisaṃhitā*.
The twentieth chapter is completed.
Now begins the twenty-first chapter:
"Having tasted the sweet [water], there are twenty; thus, four [rivers] flow from the single [lake]."
On the seventeenth [verse], it is said that there are four, eight, and one;
the twelfth belongs to Vāyu, and the two and seven are the Visrutās;
furthermore, there are nine [verses] beginning with "punāti vo," and the wrapping is indeed one.
The *brahmakṣatra* consists of twenty-two verses; then there are five *ekavṛt* verses;

indeed, the *nānā* consists of twenty-three verses; there are three [verses] of four [syllables each] and one of one; the *āśvina* has ten syllables as its tenth foot; and there is one *ekavṛt* verse with twenty-one syllables.
On the fifteenth day, he established *tejaḥ* with six *visarjanīya*s;
and on the fourteenth day, he [established] *vyāghrām*, *visrug*, and likewise *ekam*.
When he milked on the fourteenth day, there was one for each of the two and three.
The twelve [verses] are for the sacrifice and the two-fold dismissal;
the eleventh is the form of initiation, and the second is the two-fold dismissal.
The eleventh is the form of the three, and four are declared as the three.
The form of Soma is proclaimed as two coils on the twelfth day;
on the eleventh day, there is one in the form of a throne, and there may be four or three;
on the thirteenth day, there is one for the altar and the sacrificial post, and likewise two increases.
The Havirdhāna [is formed] by the twelfth; the Visrastras are three and the Visrutas are three;
by the Praiṣas there are ten Praiṣas; then eight, six, and two;
from the ten animals, the animals [are formed]; four [are formed] from the Vṛt and Śalad [sections], two each.

The parched grains (dhānāḥ) and the groats (karambhaḥ) are for the twelfth; here, with six [verses], the form of the parched grains is expressed by ten, and the form of the two [other offerings] is declared by two. On the thirteenth day, three [offerings] of curd-mixture (payasaḥ) flow forth in succession.
On the eleventh day, "āśrā vaye" is [the first]; likewise, there are five verses for the Pañcavṛt, and five for the fifth [stotra].
For the ten [days], there are three verses for the Ṛcīndhānas, and the fifth is indeed [the same].
The morning pressing belongs to the Aśvins; for the ten [days], there is one [verse] in the Triṣṭubh.
With the Vāyavya verses on the eleventh day, one [cup] is offered in the same manner;
with the Yajus formulas on the twelfth day, the fifth and ninth [cups] are offered once each. Then, with the nine Ilā-verses, there are six and two draughts for the two [days].
Through the vow one attains initiation; again, by twelve steps [one reaches] fourteen; such is the form, with the *visarjanīya* as the single [syllable];
the fifteenth is *surāvantam*, and the fifth is desired as the sixth.
That which is its essence consists of the seventeenth, as well as the single, the fourth, the seven,
the fourteenth, the twin Aśvins, and each one individually;
that which is here the eighteenth when satisfied, and indeed the three dismissals.
"svadhā namas" for the ancestors, the fourth [mantra], and likewise the seventh;
"akṣan pitaraḥ" is the seventh, while three are for the dismissal (*visarjana*);
"punantu mā" is the eleventh, the second [is for the ancestors], and four are for the dismissal (*visruk*).
May the Ekādaśī purify me; may the two on the Vṛddha and three on the Trayodaśī purify me;
may the two on the Dvādaśī, the two on the Vṛddha, and the three as declared purify me;
may I be purified by the Pavitra with ten and one, until the end.
That which is yours on the Pavitra-ekādaśī consists of one *vṛtta* and likewise six;
from both [of these], with nine deities, there is one *vṛtta* and two *visruk*s.
On the Vaiśvadevī-saptadaśī, there are three *vṛtta*s and six in the *sva*s.
Those which are equal to twelve on the twelfth day, and to six on the two days of increase;
on the eleventh day among the living and the non-living, there are four; in the Visrūg [day] there is one;
nine and ten, two, and two Sutīs respectively.
This oblation consists of the twenty-third [hymn], the ninth *vṛkta* as the fourth; "udīratām" with the nineteenth as the first;
likewise "tvam soma" with the nineteenth; two [hymns] with four [verses each]; and the four renowned [hymns].
May you slay twenty; then with two [arrows], eight for each of the two; and you, O Soma, on the seventeenth day, four and three are poured forth;
twenty are the Barhiṣads, while two and six are poured forth by Vṛtra.
On the seventeenth [verse] of the *upahūta* section, from two [verses] they take three; on the nineteenth, one; he recites for the Pitṛs four [verses], four, and two;
the Agniṣvātta [Pitṛs] know the sixteenth [section] as five, and the fifth [section] as five.
Let the seventeen come to us—the three sevens and the two;
in the fifteenth [stotra] there are the Agniṣvātta Pitṛs, the fivefold, and the fourth is the sixteenfold;
the Agniṣvātta Pitṛs are accompanied by the Nṛtūts, fourfold, and sixfold in one.
Twenty [verses] ending with *ācyājānu*, five *visarjanas* for the two [next sections],
seventeen for the *āsīnāsaḥ*, and one for the fourth vow (*vrata*);
"O Agni, Kavyavāhana," on the fourteenth day, three [sections] by three [verses].
The Agni hymn on the Kavya-Pañcadaśī consists of four, six, one, and nine verses; "tvam agne īḷita" has three, four, and one;
this [hymn] for the Pitṛs has twenty, three, and six verses, which are indeed well-known.
Those which are twenty-five here, forty in four [sections], and two;
then nine, ten, one, eight, and two;
then "uśantas tvā" on the fourteenth [day], with three omissions and two at the end.
On the eleventh day, the emissions from the foam of the waters occurred in six stages according to sequence;
King Soma was born on the nineteenth day, and the tree became one, four, and then twenty-four; from the waters, milk flowed for five and seven days.
Semen and urine [are assigned] on the thirteenth; two are declared for the two enclosures (vṛti), and three for the thirteenth day.
In the form of the visible (dṛṣṭa-rūpa) there are four, and then four in the two by means of the Veda. In the sixteenth [day], there are four, and four for each enclosure.
The lead-tantra is the fifteenth; having joined them together, there are twenty-one.
That form consists of two and eight. Then the Aśvins are the fifteenth; likewise, three and one make four. Visruk is three.
Sarasvatī is on the seventeenth; there is one [verse] for the three *sukra* cups;
with milk on the seventeenth, there is one [verse] for ghee and three for the *trayaḥ*; the *ṣoḍaśin* cup has two; *mitra* and *sutrāman* have three and one respectively.
Nine intestines, two cooking-pots,
six at the joints, one jar, eight Maniṣṭhus, eighteen, four, ten, and one mouth; twenty-two for the Sadasya, five Visruks, and one Nāntaka.
On the seventeenth day, the two Aśvins were given the eyes; on the fifteenth, the sheep was given by five;
on the sixteenth, the ram was given by two; on the seventh, the semen was taken from Indra; the eighteenth was his form, and there were three emissions.
In the self consisting of nine and ten, there are two in the organ of generation; then, from two by two, there are two.
The limbs in the self are eighteen and one; through four, there is oneness.
Sarasvatī is the woman; eighteen, thirteen, and two—there is oneness.
The *tejaḥ* of the cattle is in the *ṣoḍaśī*; three [stotras] and likewise the fifth;
the *ṣoḍaśī* is the navel of the *kṣatra*; one [stotra] and four are renowned as belonging to the *saptadaśī*; the *āśvina* is the remedy for two; and there is one for *vṛtra*.
On the ninth day, there is one *krośika*; on two [days], two;
on the seventeenth, one; on the seventeenth, two;
with four and seven, the *jihvāmebhadraka* on the sixteenth, two, and likewise eight.
On the twelfth day, my two arms and one strength are desired there as one;
on the fifteenth, my nourishments are four, and the [four] quarters are fourfold;
on the fourteenth, my navel is [established], and then the two enclosures by the five.
On the fourteenth day, one should worship with two verses on the two shanks; likewise, two on the two [thighs]; six on the limbs, one on the self (the heart), and one on the feet.
Then, on the thirteenth day, three deities are worshipped with three verses and again with nine.

The first, second, and twelfth [verses], two [verses] on the ninth, the *visruk* [verse], and seventeen [verses] along with the *sāmans* and *ṛks*; the seventeenth, the seventh, and the thirteenth; on the fifteenth day, the body hairs; on the twenty-fifth day, the fifth *visruk*.
Thus ends the twenty-first chapter in the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the *Vājasaneyisaṃhitā*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
Now begins the twenty-second chapter.
If on the thirteenth day there is one *vṛta* with five [syllables],
and if on the fourteenth day and subsequent days there are three *visargas*,
and if on the fourteenth day while awake there are three *visarjanīya*s;
On the twelfth day, one should recite the *Ṛyapaka* hymn; then, on the two [next] days, one *Vṛca* each.
On the twelfth day, one should recite the three verses beginning with *drupadādiva*. On the five [next] days, the *Visrutāḥ* hymns are recited.
On the thirteenth day, one should recite the *udvayaṃ* hymn; likewise, four [verses] on each of the four [subsequent] days.
Today, thirty-four waters have come together as one;
twenty-five and four from two [groups], and seventeen I add to two; thus two and one are desired.
In that [verse] where there are two *visargas* combined in the seventeenth [syllable] belonging to Brahmā;
wherein Indra [has] four *visarjanas* in the seventeenth;
in the thirteenth [there is] "śunā tem"; "śuḥ" is the fifth, and thereafter is "visruk".

They sprinkle and pour out on the thirteenth day; [there are] parched grains and eight [portions] of groats with two [verses], excluding the *visrug* day. On the twelfth day, there are two [verses] for Indra; but on the [thirteenth] day, one [verse] for each of the three.
O Adhvaryu, there should likewise be two sets of ten with the initial [verses];
that which is the nineteenth among beings is the single *vṛt*; then for the two groups of six, and for the Prāṇapa, on the thirteenth [day], there are six *vṛts* here by means of nine.
Of that which was performed in the ninth month of Āśvina, the fifth and the one following it were kindled by Indra; with the *ṣoḍaśī* [stotra], the sixth and eighth [verses] of the *ṣaḍvṛc* [hymn];
and with the *narāśaṃsa*, four, six, and two [verses] in the *ṣoḍaśī*.
The *ṣoḍaśin* was joined by the gods with the fifth [verse], while enjoying the oneness of the five,
nine, and one; the *ṣoḍaśin* [verse] is the ninth with the fifth,
and Indra is the door-keeper with the seventeenth, likewise the twelfth of the three.
In the fifteenth [laud], there are five *ṛca*s with the *anaktā* verses; in the sixteenth, there is oneness through the six *vṛt* verses.
Measuring out the sixteenfold [laud], there are two [verses] in the seventeenth; three [verses] are oneness, and the three goddesses are oneness with the seven *vṛt* verses.

Tvaṣṭṛ placed eighteen; and one [was added] from three, so that the Vanaspati became seventeen. From two [there were] six, but by means of six there was oneness; the fifteenth [verse] belongs to the drops, and from two [there were] seven flowing forth.
May Indra come with twenty-three; the eighth is Visrūka Āna;
Indra is the eighteenth, and the fifth and eighth are Ekata and Navadaśya Āna; Indra is indeed four, and again five.
On the seventeenth [verse], *trātāram* is desired as four; on the two [verses following], it is desired as two.
On the fourteenth, *indraḥ sutrāmā* is six; with seven, there is unity.
Of that, we are eighteen; there are four, and there is unity of four.
In the first period, there are nine, ten, eight, three, four, two, and two;
in the second, twenty; in the fourth, eighteen; in the seventh, fourteen;
in the sixth, two or seventeen; and in the eighth, twenty-one. These are the durations of the periods.

On the twelfth [verse], there are two *tanūnapāt* verses; on the eleventh, however, there is one *aikāhika* verse addressed to Indra. Then, for the verses addressed to Sarasvatī, there is one [verse] in sequence;
on the thirteenth, there is one *ājuhvānā* verse, and here there are two *vṛddha* verses.
Thirteen [verses] belong to the Aśvins; some say [they belong to] Anumati. On the fourteenth day, there is one observance (*vrata*) for the Kavaṣas. By three [days], five [verses] are said to be one;
on the eleventh day, Uṣas and Night [are celebrated], and three [verses] and four [verses] are one.
May the Aśvins protect us by day— the fourteenth, the eleventh, the threefold three, the twelfth, the pair, and the two;
may the Aśvins consume the thirteen, consume the one, and [consume] in the three streams.
On the eleventh day, there is the Ṛtuja and Indra; on the twelfth, three [offerings] with the fourth being the Vṛddhi;
on the thirteenth, "gobhir naḥ" and one for Trayī; he performed one for each; on the fourteenth, the Aśvins; and on the fifteenth, two for the dismissal of the oblation (havirvisarga).
Yama and the Aśvins on the thirteenth day have one *visṛk* and one *ekana*;
Indra, however, on the thirteenth day has three *visargas*.
And *ya indra*, *indra*, and *dvādaśī* have two sets of three, and the sixth [day] likewise.
Savitṛ [bestowed] the twelfth [day], and Varuṇa [bestowed] one; they two increased the Vṛddhi. Varuṇa [bestowed] sovereignty on the twelfth, and he cut away one and a second.
The Aśvins, renowned for their cattle, [bestowed] eleven, and those two [bestowed] one.
The two Aśvins [spoke] on the eleventh day; three [spoke] on that same day;

one [spoke] on the twelfth day with those two as physicians; four [spoke]; and three said, "O you two, the *surā* [is offered] on the eleventh day; by means of two [verses], however, one [verse] is praised."
On the fourteenth day, there is no dog; on the fifteenth, the four are one;
O Agni, on the seventeenth day, there are six for the vow; if on the twelfth, it is by the splendor of the two Āśvins; and on the thirteenth, it is indeed the renowned.
With ten *gomadgu* [verses], one brings four and one;
with six, nine, ten, and three;
and with nine, two and two—that is what is to be brought down.
The *pāvakānassa* [verse] has eight syllables; with two [syllables] there is a *vṛtti*, and with three it is *visruk*.

It is the impeller (*codayitrī*) of pleasant truths (*sūnṛtānām*). There may be seven [syllables] for one *vrata*, while the great ocean (*maho arṇaḥ*) consists of ten [syllables]; likewise, there are four *visrut*s.
O Citrabhānu, come with ten Indras; likewise, two, four, seven wise ones impelled by devotion, two surrounded, and four;
then, hastening, eight, and one surrounded as the fourth.
"The Aśvins [beginning] with the eleventh, and three and one proceed"—
thus ends the twenty-second chapter in the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
Now begins the twenty-third chapter:
on the twelfth day, one verse beginning with "imaṃ me varuṇa" is prescribed; on the seventeenth day, one verse beginning with "tvanno agne"; and on the sixth day, there is likewise a single [verse].
The *Satvanas* [are praised] with twenty-one verses; those renowned for their power with two; on the fifteenth [day] they were upon the great earth; five times they chose as they knew;
the Sutrāman [is praised] with fifteen verses; and the fourth [verse] was indeed chosen.

On the seventh day, one mounts the boat; on the eighth, the *vṛhat* and *rathantara* [sāmans]; on the ninth, the *mitra*; likewise, one [verse] on the eleventh; two [verses] on the twelfth for the *vṛddhi* and *viṣṇugdvaya*;
on the twentieth, the *prabāhu*, the *vāsi*, and the *sraj*; and there are two *visarjana*s.
The *samiddha* [verse] is on the twelfth [day], the *visruk* on the fourteenth with nine [syllables],
the *tanūnapāt* on the twelfth, and likewise the *catuḥṣaṣṭi* on the thirteenth; Agni is present in two [verses] with eleven [syllables].
On the twelfth day, Agni Subarhis has four;
on the fifteenth, the goddess Dvāra has nine and one;
and on the fourteenth, Uṣas has eleven and six others; and here, Vṛtra has five.
The two divine Hotṛs [are in the first]; one in the thirteenth; three in the fourfold-unified [set];
Ilā in the fifteenth; likewise one again with eight;
Tvaṣṭṛ in the fourth; thirteen in the three; and Vṛtra in the six.
On the fourteenth day, one [verse] is recited for Śamitāna;
on the thirteenth day, two [verses] are said for Yajña; on the seventh, Vṛta;
on the twelfth, by means of the Vasanta [season]; and on the sixth, two [verses] according to the rule.
In the summer, there is one on the thirteenth day and one on the sixth;
likewise, with the rains, there is one on the thirteenth and one on the sixth;
and with the autumn, there is one on the thirteenth and one on the sixth.
By Hemanta, thirteen [verses] on the thirteenth day and likewise one on the eighth;
by Śaiśira, thirteen [verses] on the thirteenth day and then one on the eighth;
the Hotṛ shall sacrifice with nineteen [verses], and there two on the tenth day in succession.
Tanūnapāt is seventeen; Catvār-iṣa is sixty-four;
Narāśaṃsa is twenty-one; then two [make] eighteen;
Visruk is twenty; and the two Vṛtis together with six make one.
The *barhis* is woolly; with two [verses] one cuts four [stalks], the doors and the quarters are twenty-four;
and for three [verses], there are ten indeed, along with twenty well-formed ones in three turns, and then for two.
The two divine Hotṛs are eighteen; the two renowned ones likewise;
the three goddesses; twenty-one; and seven in sequence;
the one with good seed; twenty-four in two; and sixty-four in four.
One for Vanaspati, one for Savitṛ, seventeen for each [deity],
forty-five for Agni, four *svāhā* offerings in the eighth [offering],
twenty-four for the Aśvins, two goats, and twelve for the *visarjana* offerings.
The Aśvins have forty-four; the Samiṃ has twenty-one;
the Aśvins have fifty-eight; the Chāga has ten; the Vṛddhāsva has twenty;
the Vanaspati has forty-eight; and the Abhijit has seven.
There are fourteen *visargas*, and here one is said to end in *n*.
There are nine, ten, and three for *agni-sviṣṭakṛt*; seven are the *visarga-nās*.
For the deity *barhis* on the seventeenth [verse], there are three and five.
The *devīs* are fourteen; the *dvāras* are one, four, and likewise fourteen; the *uṣāsas* are two, and the fourth is one;
the *joṣṭrīs* are fourteen; and for three [of these], there are three and one.
On the seventeenth day, there is the *jāhiti* of the moon; on the sixth day, there are four *ṣoḍaśīs*.
Among the gods, there are three *vṛcch* and two *visruk*s.
There are three goddesses on the fifteenth day, and one *veṣṭana* with five [verses].
The god Indra is eighteen-fold; let there be three in the sixth [section].
The god is twenty-one-fold with the gods, and again ten-fold by four.
The god is nineteen-fold on the outside; let there be four three-fold [sections].

Agni Sviṣṭakṛt is the forty-fourth deity; there are twelve [syllables], fourteen [in] the Visarga, and the final one is *m*; two are uttered at the end, twenty-three for Agni today, and four and two in the sixth.
"Five well-established [syllables], twenty-five, four, seven, three respectively;
forty-four today, O Sage, six increased by ten"—
thus [ends] the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the *Vājasaneyisaṃhitā*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
The twenty-third chapter is completed.
Now begins the twenty-fourth chapter: "Tejosi," "Śukram," ten [syllables], one, four, and likewise four.
They grasped eighteen [syllables] as the first; one and one as the third;
you are named after the fifteenth; four indeed are the fourth;
for Prajāpati, twenty-eight is desired, with five, five, and one.
The Ekādaśī, the Arvanta, the Visargas as the fifth,
"Svāhā to Agni," "to Soma," the Padāc, the twelve Hiṃkāras, and likewise eight Veṣṭanas in sequence.
For *niviṣṭāya*, there are eight *upaviṣṭa*s; for *samāpyale*, three *vṛta*s; likewise for *kūjate*, eight; for *prabuddhāya*, seven *vṛccha*s;
for *yate* in the eighth [section], "dhāvata" and so on, there are three *vṛta*s separately.
For Javāyu, the eighth [verse] from the *balā* hymn; likewise, four for Vṛta on the twelfth day; for Īkṣamāṇa, two verses from the *rathantara*;
for Hiraṇyapāṇi, the ninth verse from the *vṛc* hymn; and likewise one for each [of the remaining deities].

Then, from the verse beginning with *devasya*, there are eight and two, making two pairs; from the eight verses beginning with *suṣṭutiṃ*, three and two are desired; and again, from the three verses beginning with *satpatiṃ*, the selection (*vṛtam*) is made.
Of the god Savitṛ and Tvaṣṭṛ there are two [verses] each; then one for each; with the *stoma* of Agni there are nine, and one and two more;
with the *sahavyavāt* there are ten, and again two and six.
Having passed the tenth [day], O you whose back is dripping with ghee, three and one, then one more; on the eleventh day, Agni, Indu, and one, and one again, and once more as one— verily,
he generated [the world] by means of ten, and indeed by three of the three.
Vibhū has twenty-two syllables; Daśama likewise [has] three; the Devas [have] seven; Āśā [has] seventeen; Vṛc [occurs] in three and six;
and Kāyaka [has] nine, four, and one.
For Aditi Mahī there are six; here, however, one is surrounded by four. For Pūṣan there are four, and likewise for Prapathyamya.
By the thirteenth [verse], O Brahman, the Brahman [priest] is established in three, five, and one.
The *dogghrī* [is on] the *thenu*; on the seventeenth day, two are said to be eight and one;

on the *nikāma* [day], which is the eleventh, there is one; furthermore, the seventh of the three is again [on] the seventh of the *prāṇa* and *apāna*, as well as once for each of the two functions (*vṛtti*).
One should perform [the rites] for the eastern direction, the speech, the southern direction, and likewise the ten-footed [earth];
for water and the waters, the twelfth; and again, two enclosures with nine [verses each];
for the wind and the smoke, eighteen; one should perform these twice in the fifth [section].
For Agni on the eleventh day there is one *vṛt* in two [verses];
for the Visruk Nakṣatras on the ninth day there are seven *visrugs* in two [verses];
and for Indra and Sūrya there are three *vṛts*, with the seventh being a *vṛt*.

From the six roots and the branches, one should offer one oblation; likewise, one to the Earth, one to the Intermediate Space on the twelfth day, one to the Three on the seventh, one to Asu and Vasu on the eighth, and five windings are prescribed.
For *śūṣāya* there is the *saṃsarpa*, and for *sapta* the *veṣṭana*; likewise, for *nadave* and *mādhavāya*, there are thirteen [verses] each;
on the fourteenth day, for *vāja*, there are six, and for *vrata* there is one *visruta*.
"Āyu with twenty [syllables], yajña with four, and likewise ekādaśa with eleven;
in the seventh [section] one [syllable] for him, and by two [syllables] three are encompassed, and then one more"—
thus it is stated in the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the *Vājasaneyisaṃhitā*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
The twenty-fourth chapter is completed.
Now begins the twenty-fifth chapter:
"Twenty-six [verses] for Prajāpati; three; he who is the five-in-oneness."
He who [knows] the twelve from the breath (*prāṇataḥ*), and the nine and eighteen that have flowed forth;
the moon remains as the nineteenth, and there is a prolation (*pluta*) over two syllables.
They join the *vraghna* with nine, and the single *visarjanīya* [is joined] with nine.
On the ninth [verse], they yoke his four steeds in succession:
"yadvāto," "apa" on the sixteenth, "visruk," and the five ending in "ekanā.
"pavasvasvām," "jantu," and "nanmeka" occur in three verses; these are the *visṛbhāḥ*.
"Bhūr bhuvaḥ svar," the seventeenth [syllable], and one [syllable] for each of the two [next verses];
the seventeenth [syllable] for some; alone, the fourth; three [syllables] for Visruka;
Sūrya alone on the twelfth day; by two [syllables] for Vṛc, but the fifth.
The seventeenth [hymn] was by Kaśvīd; likewise, one [hymn] by the two [Kaśvīd and Kaśyapa];
on the thirteenth day, one [hymn] by Dyau; but on the sixth day, those who were renowned [performed]:
[one hymn] with ten verses, and one by Pāyu; and the seventh was Visruk.
This is the meaning: on the sixteenth day, there is no unity between the two; on the eleventh, there is unity with the [first] ten; but on the sixth, there is separation from the seventh;
or on the thirteenth, the three *vājins* themselves are one, yet not the last is one.
The twenty-third and the ninth; the fourth consists of five parts;
Agni is the sacrificial animal with twenty-two [syllables]; the Visargas and the teeth are one by one;
"O Mother, O Ambika" on the twelfth; two for each, and again two for the Vṛc.
On the eleventh day, one should worship you, the Lord of the Gaṇas, with five separate enclosures.
On the sixth day, I am the twenty-second [deity], and on the fifth [day] there are five;
as for the evening of the eleventh, it is unified through two and three.
The *yakāsaka* and *śakuntikā* are [the first two]; the thirteenth is the *visruta*;
the fifteenth consists of the two *yakāsakas*; the fifth is chosen from among the two;
and the mother is on the seventeenth; however, one *visrut* is praised.
The Mother is the seventeenth; one enclosure (vṛta), three unities (ekatā);
above this, on the fourteenth [day], two enclosures and two non-ends (anantaka).
Above this, however, fourteen, an enclosure, and a pair of two non-ends.
Of this [lunar day], on the twelfth, there are four *catasraka*s;
on the twelfth, whatever these [deities] are, there are likewise three for two [days];
and on the fourteenth, that which is *hariṇa* consists of one *vṛt* and one *eka*.
In the sixteenth [verse], that which is *hariṇam* has three *visargas* mentioned;
in the thirteenth, *dadhikrāvṇaḥ* has five [syllables] and likewise the *vaiṣṭambha*;
in the twelfth, there are two *gāyatrīs*, one *triṣṭubh*, and one [more].
On the fourteenth day of the month of Dvipadā, there was one Visruk with six verses;
there were eleven Mahānāmans and three Navas; the thirteenth was Nāri; that was the fifth Visarga.
Twelve silver [pieces], nine deer-skins, and eight lead [pieces];
who covers you? Seventeen and one; surrounded by five;
the seasons are twelve, and one surrounded by three is proclaimed.
The twelve half-months are your joints; there are four in each pair.
By the divine fourteen-day path, one is encompassed on the fifth day.
Heaven is your back, and the fifteen-fold earth provides a set of four for some.
In the fifteenth [day], there are three others; indeed, by five, what is it? O Sūrya, the fifteenth belongs to two, and three belong to two;
the fourteenth is Brahma-Sūrya; two are surrounded, and the fifth is oneness.
I ask you: nine and ten again make two;
twenty is the pair separated from those three; and one and two are chosen among them.
In which [numbers] would there be an end to twenty? And how is the oneness of four and two?
On the ninth day, there are five within the five; five are covered and five are flowing. Then, on the tenth day, there is the *kāram* and the *mareṣolaśī*; these two are for the two increases.
Then, on the eleventh day, there is the twentieth for the goat; and on the twelfth day, there is the flow for three and two.
How many [verses] are assigned to this [hymn]? Eighteen are distributed among three [stanzas], and five are distributed among five;
nine and ten are distributed among six, and seven and three are distributed among seven.
Who knows this? The seventeenth [verse] belongs to it, and the seventh indeed belongs to two.
I know his sixteenfold [nature], as well as the three and the three; I ask you about the eighteenth, the one supreme, and the fifth.
I know the nineteenth, the Veda, the one chosen, and the ten-fold [manifestation].

"Thirteen is *subhūḥ* itself; here, three [are formed] with seven; the Hotṛ sacrificed for the creatures; ten and one; the second is chosen"—thus [ends] the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the Vājasaneyisaṃhitā composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
The twenty-fifth chapter is completed.
Now begins the twenty-sixth chapter:
"On the thirteenth day, tomorrow, [the offering of] a hornless goat; and indeed three on the seventh."
The twelve Aśvinas, the two Rāmas below, one Vṛta with seven [verses],
the two Tvaṣṭras, Loma’s twenty-one, six Vṛcas, and thirteen;
Śitirandhra on the fifteenth day, eight Vṛcas, and likewise twelve.
On the thirteenth day of the bright fortnight, there are five; on the ninth, nine; on the Visruk, nine;
on the Avalidhā, four; on the Raudra, nine; on the ninth, the Visruk;
on the tenth, the Phalguna; on the Lohitāṇī, four; on the Vṛddha, seven.
The sixth [set] consists of six [cows] with black necks and white teeth; then the eighth is surrounded by eight;
the twelfth belongs to the Viśvedevas; likewise, the fourth and the eighth consist of black-necked ones;
and on the eleventh day, there is another group of four swift [cows].
The sixteenth is the *ṛṣabha*, while the fifth is the fourteenth;
these eleven are dedicated to Indra and Agni. Two are for Vṛtra, and likewise the twelfth;
those with black necks are for the thirteen, while ten are distributed among the three.
The eighth and tenth lunar days of the earth (Bhauma) are Kṛṣṇā; the ninth is Visarga;
and Dhūmā is on the fourteenth. Visrugdeva and Pañcanāntaka [occur] on the tenth, for the conjunction of the three parts, from the seventh through the five transits.

On the tenth day, there is the sixth offering; on the fifth day, there are three offerings of black-necked goats and the *ṣoḍaśī* cup; on the fourth day, the *ṣoḍaśin* and the *viṣuvant*; the tenth day is concluded with the *saṃcara* and the *ṛc*, and there are ten *viṣruṭ* offerings.
For Agni Nīkagras, fourteen [verses] are prescribed; for the tenth and fifth [days], five;
on the eighth, the *saṃcara* verses are stated; likewise, from the fifth, the eighth;
the smoky-colored (*dhūmra*) ones on the fifteenth day of the brown (*babhru*) period; then the ninth in the sixfold cycle (*ṣaḍvṛt*).
The transits have been stated: one on the eighth,
eight on the fourteenth, one for the spring, two on the fifteenth,
twelve on the twelfth, and the fifth on both [the first and the ninth].
For Soma, on the twelfth day, there is a *haṃsa* [meter]; with two [syllables], one [verse] is the fourth;
for Agni on the twelfth day, there are the *kūṭarūn*; and in the enclosure (*vṛti*), there is one on the fifth day;
for Soma, *lanrāṃ* on the fourteenth day; *tra-tri*, four, and three.

On the fourteenth day, [the offering is] for Parāvata; on the two [following days], for Ṣaḍbhṛt; likewise, on the three [following days], for Bhūmi; on the twelfth day, for Ākhu; on the two [following days], however, for Pañcamī;
on the thirteenth day, one [offering] for the Vasus; on the sixteenth day, for Ṛśyā; and then five [offerings] on the fifth [set of days].
The twelfth [verse] is for Śānāyapa; one [verse] for Visrūp; four for Prajāpati on the eleventh day; two with one [verse]; then three;
twenty-four for Prajāpati; and six for Vāyu on the eighth.
The mayu belongs to Prajāpati with eighteen [verses]; then four [belong] to the Ekādaśin; the kuluṅga for Soma with nineteen;
the fourth is the balākā for Surya with twenty; then four with nine.
The *suparṇa* has twenty [verses], the *pārjanya* has four, the *puruṣamṛga* has thirteen, and the *trayodaśa* has eighteen; for three [hymns] there are ten *visrutā*s,
and for the eight [days] of the *eṇya* day, the second *maṇḍala* follows in sequence.
The *anya-vāpa* consists of eighteen; the *tri-ṣṭubh* consists of three sevens;
the *varṣāhū* consists of nineteen; the *dvādaśa-visrutā* consists of two twelves;
the *śvitra* consists of eighteen *ādityas*; the *vṛt* consists of one ten and one one.
The *Khadga*, the *Vaiśvadeva*, the twenty-one-fold, the eleven-fold, and the twelve-fold *Viśruk*—
thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter in the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the *Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
Now begins the twenty-seventh chapter:
"With teeth, [there are] twenty śādas; in the sixth [verse], there is oneness in five;
with the beard, twenty Ādityas; and likewise, oneness in four ṛṣads."
The wind [is established] in the vital breath; the twenty-first is surrounded by nine and flows through nineteen; from the two ears come nineteen; the fifth unity is with five;
there may be mosquitoes on the thirteenth; thirty-three are desired with three.
Having chanted the *java* verses on the fourteenth day, one [verse] for each of the three *veṣṭas*;
twenty-six for Agni; two for the two wings; eight for the *visrutās*;
thirty-two for Indra and Agni; and likewise three for each of the ten wings.
There are twenty-four sections for the Maruts; three for the Vicaturas;
twenty-two for Pūṣan; six for Urva; five for Aṣṭu; five for Indra; twelve for Kroṣṭu; one for Vṛka; and likewise two and one.
The *nabha* has twenty-two [verses], the *udarya* has forty-six, and the fifth is the *vidhṛti*.
From the *nābhya*, there are twenty-six; three are *vṛcca*, and eight are *visruta*.
Of these four, eighteen belong to the *vṛccatasraka*.

The *Āptoryāma* consists of eighteen [verses], the fourth [of the *Ṣoḍaśin*] is the fifth; the *Visruk* is the ninth [verse] of the nine, four [verses] for the eleven, and the *Ekata* belongs to the gods. The *Bhadra* is the twenty-first, and the *Vela* is by two [verses] among the six.
The nineteenth [verse] from those [preceding ones], doubled by the first two, becomes one;
that [is the twenty-first], and the wind [is] in the three [verses] with the eight dismissals;
him, the Lord, the nineteenth, the chosen one, indeed the fifth.

"May it be well with us; Indra [is praised] in the *ṣoḍaśī* [stotra], three [verses] in the *vṛddha-daśāvisruk*, and the *pṛṣadaśva-ṣoḍaśī* has five [verses]; the *ekavṛd* [stoma] consists of eleven [verses];
'Bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ' [is recited] in the *saptadaśī* [stotra], and then nine [verses] in the *trivṛt*."
One hundred and twenty-one [verses] form one [hymn], and again one [verse] forms the eighth [hymn];
Aditi and Dyaus [form] nineteen [verses], and Visruk [forms] twelve [verses] with an increase of one;
Mitra is eighteen [verses], but there is a unity among the ten [verses] in two places.
That which is the washing consists of seventeen; the three rams with six;
this goat consists of eighteen, twice six, and indeed eight;
and that which is the oblation consists of eighteen, three, and eight in unity.

The Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu are the fifteenth; at the sixth [rite] there are six, but here the wood-cutters are the eighteenth; four of the six [verses], likewise "upaprāgāt" and so on, are twenty; and for three [verses], there is a group of four.
If the horse has twenty-three [vessels], there are two [types] and three courses;
if the horse has twenty-two, one [type] is renowned in three courses;
if it is the seventeen [vessels] to be slain, four [types] are renowned in three courses.
That which [flowed] from his limbs was twenty-one-fold; three and two were the outpourings.
The horse was twenty-one-fold; with five and with six [he performed the rites]. The inspection was sixteen-fold; again, three and five.
Having measured with twenty-one [verses] for the fire-paths, he makes four strides with three;
the stepping-out is twenty, and for the three [verses], one more;
when there are fifteen [verses] for the horse, there are three chosen ones and twenty-one strides.
"Twenty-eight [verses] for these [sections], nine [verses] from the five [preceding ones].
Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter in the *Padakārikā Ratnamālā* on the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
Now begins the twenty-eighth chapter:
Twenty fires, the earth, and again the eighth of the four;
on the thirteenth day, those with desire, three, two, and then unity.
Brahmarāja is one dynasty, and likewise there are four Visargas;
Bṛhaspati is the twenty-sixth, while there are three [others] and indeed three more;
Indragoma is twenty, and the group of six consists of four and one.
On the fifteenth day, one [verse] for the *ṛtavān* [deity] is proclaimed for Vṛtra;
there are eight for Vaiśvānara, and that [total] becomes one with the *visarga*;
and for Agni with the *uktha*, there are three, along with one *visarga*.
The fourteenth [verse] belongs to Vaiśvānara; the fourteenth of the two [next] belongs to the Saptadaśa-stoma.
"Marutvān Indra" is the eighteenth; the unity of the two increases by two.
The eleventh [verse], "mahām̐ indro vajrī," thus belongs to the Trivṛt-stoma of the two.
Agni is the seer; likewise, there are eight, three, and four here, with sixteen through six *anuvīras*, and similarly with three and seven;
the Ānoga lineage consists of twenty, four, and seven as one.
Thus ends the twenty-eighth chapter in the *Padakārikā Ratnamālā* on the *Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
Now begins the twenty-ninth chapter.
The *samāḥ* [verse] has eighteen; the *vṛka* [verse] has one; the *visrutāḥ* [verses] are twenty-seven;

the *saṃcedhya* [verse] has twenty-five; the *ekavṛd* [verse] has two; the *visrutau* [verses] have two; "tvām agne vṛṇīṣva" has eighteen; the fourth [section] has four; and the *ekatā* [verse] has one.

Right here, O Agni, is the twenty-one-fold [stoma], the three fivefold [verses] as one; through the sovereign power (*kṣatra*), in the seventeen-fold [stoma], there are the three fivefold [verses] and the three *visrūks*;
the *atijihva* is the nineteen-fold, with two fivefold [verses] and four *visrūks*.
The nine, ten, fifteen, seventeen, and nineteen; O Bṛhaspati, the eighteen, the two, and the two that are widely renowned.
In the next [verse], in the sixteenth [chapter], there are two [verses] for the Vṛc [hymns] and three as well;
and in the eleventh [chapter], the fourth [hymn] of the three is for the upward [streams];
Tanūnapāt has twenty [verses], and there are two [verses] for the five Visruṣ [streams].
With *madhvā* and *yajñam*, there is the tenth [verse]; with two [verses], the fourth;
with *acchāyam eti*, the twelfth; with one [verse], the third;
with three [verses], the thirteenth; with two [verses], the seventeenth—these are the seven *visruts*.
On the eleventh day, the goddesses of the gates chose one; five are renowned.
On the twelfth day, they chose four for him and one.
On the twelfth day, the two divine Hotṛ-priests chose one; three are renowned.
The three *devīs* are on the eleventh; likewise, there are three *visargas*. *Tannastūrī* is on the thirteenth; in two *vṛts*, there are two *visruks*.
*Vanaspate* is on the tenth; and then, in two [sections], there is a *visarga*.
O Agni, Svāhā! On the eleventh [verse] there is one *vṛta*; likewise three; "pīvo annān" is the seventeenth; likewise eight; nine; and the "ekata" [hymn];
"rāye nu yam" is twenty; twenty-four; and the "visruk" of the two *vṛtra*s.
The Vāyu [section] follows the Agni with ten; three, six, and one proceed together; twenty, three, and four constitute the fourth;
O Vāyu, these [sections] reach the tenth; two, three, and one [follow].
With twenty, one, and ten, and with fifteen, two, and three;
having yoked the steeds, Anila [is present] on the twelfth day; for two, there are two turns and three loose;
with eighteen steeds, there are three turns and six in a single unit.
"nava vāyo" on the ninth [verse], two [verses] with the *vṛti* metre and two with the *visruta*; "yena dyauḥ" on the nineteenth; likewise two [verses] in the group of six;
"yaṃ krandasī" on the thirteenth, five with the *vṛca* metre and two thereafter.
The *āpo ha* hymn is the sixteenth; likewise, the *saptaviṣṭuk* is the seventeenth; the *yaścidāpaḥ* is the twenty-first; then follows the single *navaviṣṭuk*;
the *abhitvā śūra* is the thirteenth; the two *vṛtra* hymns are the sixth.
Having bowed, on the seventeenth [verse] there are three *vṛts*; on the seventeenth [of the next], three;
on the fifteenth, however, "āmid dhi havā" is one *vṛt*, and there are indeed three.
On the nineteenth, "satvaṃ na citra," and here in the three and five [verses].
*Kayā naḥ* on the eleventh day has one *vṛt* and three *visruks*;
*kas tvā satyaḥ* on the eleventh day likewise has four *visargas*.
*Abhīṣuṇaḥ* on the ninth day, however, is said to have one *visarga*.

At each sacrifice on the fourteenth day, there are four [verses] chosen; at the sixteen-day rite, there are four [verses] for the Son of Strength (Ūrjo Napāt) by means of two [hymns]; they are well-known as four;
"Thou art the Year" is at the sixteen-day rite, and likewise three and eleven.
"pretyā etyai pañcadaśīṃ trayo vṛccaikavisrutam"—
thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter in the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
Now begins the thirtieth chapter:
one should worship Indra with *samidh* on the fourteenth day; two with *vṛt*, four with *ekatā*, and one with *tanūnapāt* on the eleventh day; and four with *vṛt* out of six.
With the *ilā* verses, Indra [receives] the tenth; with the four, six, and those flowing from the *avi*, the two *barhis* verses;
with the twelfth, the four, and those flowing from the five, the seventeenth; with the *jona-vīrya*, the two, and the *vṛc* verses, then the two sets of six.
On the thirteenth day, Uṣas and Indra; likewise, on the fifth, the Veṣṭana hymn;
on the eleventh, two [hymns] chosen together with the physician (Bhiṣaj); three [hymns] for Visrug; Ilā and Sarasvatī in six [verses]; and one [hymn] for Vṛtra and Eka-trayoviṣrug.
Tvaṣṭṛ and Indra on the ninth; four [verses] for the wrapping in sequence;
Pīyu and Joṣṭṛ on the eleventh; three [groups] of three for the unification;
"Indra svāhā" and the clarified butter on the twelfth; three [verses] for the dismissal of the twenty-five.
The *devaṃ barhiḥ* [verse] has eighteen syllables; in two [verses] there are five [syllables] flowing forth;
the *pañcadaśī* [verse] belongs to Indra; he indeed slays in two [verses]; and one is the second;
in the *uṣāsānaktā* [verse] there are eleven; then four, and two thereafter.

On the fifteenth day, two enclosures are said to be the "Vasudhiti"; there are eighteen milks from the five well-yielding cows, and four enclosures for the father; likewise, there is one enclosure for the "hatādyaśam" and one for the "vela."
Patimindra was chosen on the twelfth; Vṛccheka and Ekatā were both chosen together;
Trivarūtha was chosen on the seventeenth; four [were chosen] on the fifth;
Madhuśākha was chosen on the ninth; and Dvita was chosen on the second.
The two [verses] beginning with *stāḥ* and *sthāḥ* are for the seventh [offering];
after that, performing the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering, one should take three [verses] from the seventh [chapter] and one from the third;
then, on the twelfth day, the *visruk* [verse] is one as previously stated, beginning with *indrā yaccha*.
On the fifteenth day, one should offer to Samidhāna; four [verses] are for Tanūnapāt on the fourth [day]; to Vṛtra, nine and one;
to Iḷā, nine; to Mṛḷīka, two; and likewise one.
On the ninth [verse], however, there are three *vṛt* for the *subarhiṣ*; likewise, on the tenth, there are three *svatīs*. But for the *supra*, there are six *trayāvṛts*;
on the ninth, however, there are eight *vṛc*s for the *supeśas*, and so on in that sequence.
And by Pracetas, ten [verses] were seen; four and one by Vita;
the Peśasvatīs on the eleventh day; one by Vṛdha; the Saptaviśrutās; "Sureta" on the ninth day; and indeed three Veṣṭanas.
The *hiraṇyaparṇa* with nine [verses] is called one binding;
the *svāhākṛti* is one, and there are four *catasraka*s.
"Śuci, muṣṇihā, eighteen, seven, vṛt, three, and e"—
thus ends the thirtieth chapter of the *Padakārikāratnamālā* on the Vājasaneyi-Saṃhitā, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
Now begins the thirty-first chapter: Then,
on the nineteenth day, three [applications] with ghee, two, and the fourth.
Barhis, Ṣoḍaśī, Dvyaśvatvāris, Visrutās,
and Enāveṣṭana as the fifth.
Of the first [verses], there are three turns of sixteen; and in the nineteenth, eight [turns] of seventeen.
In the two [next], twenty-one.
Of Prajāpati, however, there are sixteen; one chooses four,
two for Viṣuketu, and two for the Visarjanas.
On the seventeenth [verse], there are seventeen syllables; on the three following verses, there are eighteen; on the next, there are seventeen; and on the fourteenth, there are twenty-one.
On the seventeenth [verse], there are seventeen; and on the fourteenth, there is one.
These eighteen and the fourth [soma-pressings], flowing forth in eight streams, clothe themselves in the eagle, O Seer.
Let them stand upon the chariot in the sixteenth [verse]; with two and five, let them quiet [the breath] in the twentieth; in three [verses], four and one;
"When you cried out," eighteen; for three, an increase of two in each of two.
O people, you say that Yama has one tooth;
Yama has eighteen teeth. Five and one make six;
they say you have three. With twenty and three, the fourth is one.
These indeed are seventeen; five, seven, and one for the self; the sixteenfold and the three; the twenty-five that have flowed forth;
here, for Atri, the twenty-one and the one chosen.
Twenty-one [verses] without *anuṣṭubh* or *visarga*,
seven with one less, the *Hiraṇyaśva* hymn, the seventeenth [verse], four, eleven, oneness, the *Īrmāntas*,
that [hymn] with four, nine, and the *Visrutās*.
The body of the fifteenth hymn consists of three parts; it enters into two [sections] as a single unit.
The nineteenth is proclaimed as having six emissions (*visarga*);
when there is an increase of two, the second becomes the eighteenth.
Eighteen [verses] are kindled today; four, two, and then two;
the Tanūnapāt [section] has eight, four, and three;
likewise Narāśaṃsa on the fifteenth [day]; with two increases there are five renowned [sections].
Being invoked, nineteen; three times seven; twice;
the sacrificial grass (barhis) is directed eastward; seventeen here; in three [verses], six, one;
the expansive ones are fifteen; the threefold ten are far-famed.
The *Ṣoḍaśī* is the enclosure; likewise, the tenth [verse] is the divine *hotṛ*. On the fifteenth [day], there is a group of four verses and three *visrūts*.
"Come to our sacrifice" (*ā no yajñam*) is on the nineteenth; there is one *visrūt*.
These eighteen givers— three times three, four, two, fifteen, and three times four— united as one; they became eighteen, three times three, and eightfold in renown.
Forty-one for Agni; eighteen and a sixteen-versed [hymn];
twenty-four for Agni; a black [bull]; twenty-six and six;
twenty for Agni; five-fold and nine; and one each.
Thus ends the thirty-first chapter in the *Padakārikā Ratnamālā* on the *Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
Now begins the thirty-second chapter.

On the fourteenth day there are fourteen *jarāsa* verses; on the eleventh day there are two *bṛhat* verses and eleven *visruk* verses; on the eighth day there are four *harayaḥ* verses and two *dhūmakāḥ*; on the eleventh day there are four *visrutaḥ* verses for Yajana and Mitra; likewise, on the eleventh day there is one *visruk* verse and one *ekanān*.
Two, two, and two; in the sixteenth [chapter], seven, four, and one;
three hundred and twenty-one; three, Visruka, and Trināntaka;
Agni, Vṛtrāṇi, Jaṅghā, eight, two, Vṛt, five, and the Visarjanas.
With all [the gods], the ninth verse is for Soma; one and two are for release.
For the sake of desire, the nineteenth is for Vṛtra; four are for the fourfold [sacrifice].
Agni’s strength is seventeenfold; four likewise are for unity.
For you indeed, O delightful one, are the eighteen-fold [stomas], the three Vṛtra-slayers, and the three releases; in you, O Agni, on the thirteenth day, there is the fourfold unity of the three;
hear, O performer of the hearing-rite, on the thirteenth day, there are four in the sixth.
On the thirteenth day of the Viśve-devas, there are three times seven *visarjana* chants;
Agni is the seventeenth of the great [stomas], while the fifth is a single *vṛt*.
There are twenty-three *āpas*, and the ninth *vṛt* occurs in two places.
The cows have lowed toward the tenth; one has been seized by force, one has flowed away.

When you were seen with ten, one was seized by force and three flowed away. With the ninth, pour forth for him; one has been seized by force, one has flowed away. One has been seized by force, one has flowed away.
On the seventeenth [verse], three, five, and one are desired;
the eighteenth is "pravomahem"; in the three [verses] with five [syllables each], "bṛhannididhma" is eight; "visruktim" is not at the end, [but] unity.
Indra [is mentioned] in the *himat* [hymn], and there is one [verse] in the *daśī*; Indra [is mentioned] in the fourteenth [verse], and there is unity in three [verses] among the five;
twenty-two [verses are there]; "Whence, O Indra? [is mentioned] in the eighteenth, and there is unity in the four [verses].
The *ātāna* [stoma] has eighteen verses; the *pañcavṛt* has one verse for each of two [verses];
"these twenty-four" consists of three [verses]; the *vṛd* has two [verses]; the *ekatā* has one [verse];
"shining brightly" (*vibabhrāj*) and "the great" (*bṛhat*) have eighteen [verses]; the *ṣaḍvṛt* has six [verses]; and the *visruk* has four [verses].
Nine [verses] are recommended for the *yāna* and *upāvaha*; however, one is praised for the *antya*.
With the two divine *adhvaryu* verses, there are three *veṣṭana*s.
Then, eighteen for the *ānīla-abhiṣeka*, followed by two; this is called the *vṛt-ṣal*.
Today, on the thirteenth day, the two have become one through the one; the youth has reached the ninth stage of universal maturity; the three are renowned among the two elders;
and by twenty, the four have become threefold.
The son of Navadaśī was Tanmitra; his two sons were Vṛta and Caturovisruk.
Baṇ was the son of Mahān; then from Saptadaśī came Visrugvan and three Antakas.
From Ṣaṭsūryaśravas came Ṣolaśī; from her were born four sons, two by two.
As at the end of the day one sees the sun, on the fourteenth day there is one [syllable] for the Ekādaśī; today, on the nineteenth, there are ten deities for the increase, and ten for the emission.
But with the *ākṛṣṇena* [verse] on the sixteenth day, there is one [syllable] for the increase, and then two.
On the seventeenth day, five by five, ending with one, [the waters] flowed forth; on the ninth day, Indra and Vāyu opened the single gate that ends in one;
and on the ninth, Varuṇa opened three gates among the six wide-openings.
In the ninth [day], there are two *vṛt* for Indra and two *visarjana*;
twenty for Agni and Indra; and one *vṛt* and five *visrutā*.
In the nineteenth [day], there are two *vṛt* for Indra-Agni and Mitra; and four *ekatā*.
The *asme rudrāḥ* is the sixteenth; the *pañcavṛt* consists of seven and one;
the eighteenth is *arvāñco adya*; there are two *vṛt*s with nine [verses each];
the *viśve devāḥ* is the twenty-first; and there is a unification of three into two.
For the gods, on the seventeenth day, there are two *vṛc* verses and four *visruk* verses;
here, for Vāyu, on the fifteenth day, there are six *vṛc* verses and three *visrut* verses;
on the ninth day, I invoke Mitra, as well as Veṣṭana alone.

The *dasra* [class] occurs on the eighth; for two [syllables], there is a *vṛta*; three [syllables] are separated by a pause (*visruk*); the nineteenth [class] is *vidayat*; again, two [syllables] are *vṛta*, and likewise three;
for the seventeenth [class], there is no contact (*sparśa*); for two [syllables], there are two [consonants], and for two [syllables], four.
To the fierce one, the knower of the thunderbolt, [we offer] nine and a second; in all three meters, we worship with nine; one with a *visṛk*; and then one with various [hymns].
For you indeed, in the battle for booty, [there are] twenty, seven, four, and two.
O Indra, on the seventeenth day you slew one; on the seventh, one;
on the twelfth, two; with three [days], two;
O Indra, on the fourteenth, you slew three; and four were scattered.
The hymn *a te śuṣmāḥ* consists of eighteen verses; one [hymn] was uttered for Vṛtra; eighteen [verses] were recited with the *adabdhebhiḥ*; four [verses] with the *navamī visruk*;
and on the seventeenth [verse], there are five *vṛt*s and six [verses].
In the *Kāvyas*, there are eight [syllables] in the *Rājani* meters; one each for the two *Vṛddhi* meters; the *Tiraścīna* has eighteen; the *Tisras* has eight; the *Dvināntaka* has two;
the *Ārodasī* is desired to have twenty; and the *Trīṇi* has seven, while the *Eka* has one.
In the ninth [verse], there is a second *vṛtta* with *ukthas*; in three [verses], there is unity;
with nine and ten, one more; with five, again a *vṛtta*;
"and my prayers" (*brahmāṇi me*) with twenty-one; here, two [more] with seven.
There are twenty [verses] in the Anuṣṭubh meter; three in the fourth [section];
two on the ninth and tenth; one Vṛtti; six in the Ekātā;
these [are the verses] in the Caturdaśī; and likewise four in the Aṣṭamī.

"Of which [verse] this [portion] occurs on the seventeenth [day], and one [syllable] increases; on the fourteenth [day] this [portion] is a thousand, and on the four-month [period] twenty-seven [syllables] increase"—
thus [ends] the *Padakārikā-ratnamālā* composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya within the *Vājasaneyisaṃhitā*.
The thirty-second chapter is completed.
Now begins the thirty-third chapter:
That which is before the bowstring, twenty [in number], the fourth, the three-fold enclosure, and the threefold expansion.
On the thirteenth day of the father’s *nu-stotra*, one is chosen here for increase;
on the seventeenth day of Agni-danu, the fourth is chosen as one.
O Sinīvālī, on the thirteenth day, three are chosen as the renowned one.
The thirteenth [is for] Pañcanadī; two [hymns] for Aveṣṭana; then two; then the seventeenth; "O Agni, you are the first," two [hymns]; Daśāviṣruk, twenty [hymns];
"O Agni, do thou protect us," two [hymns] for Vṛddha; the fifth [is] Viṣruk.
On the sixteenth day, we have obtained five from two;
on the thirteenth day of Ilā, we have obtained one. As we have thrice approached with the *visrug*, on the fourteenth day we have obtained two, and likewise one.
We proclaim eighteen; in the Mahānāmnī verses, they desire the eighteenth as the single unity; and in the two *vṛddhi* verses, four; in the *visruk*, one;
and likewise twenty-one, three, and three *visruk*s.
The *aṣālha* [hymn] in the *yuṣ* [section], the *ṣolaśī*, the fivefold, and the one renowned as twenty-one;
the *ṣolaśī*, the *soma*, and the *dhenu*—these two are the *vṛta*s, and the fourth is the *visarjana*.
You [should recite] these twenty [verses]; the seventh, however, is the *visarjana*.
May the twentyfold [hymn] be for us from the god; the two [verses] are the activity, and likewise the oneness.
Eight [verses] he explained; nine and ten are the activity, and the one is the fourfold oneness.
The golden-handed [Agni], with seventeen [verses], has three [stomas]; four [verses] are the threefold *viṣṭup*.
On the fourteenth day [of the month] of Hiraṇyah, seven, seven, and three [verses] are recited in sequence;
these paths number twenty, and the four renowned ones are ten;
on the ninth day, both drink, with one encircling and likewise three.
The *apnasvatī* has nineteen syllables; there two [verses] have twenty-one;

the *visruk* has eight syllables with days and nights; there two [verses] have twenty-four; the *caturaikatā* has thirty-two; the *tripārthi* has sixteen; there one [verse] has twenty-five; and the *visrutā*s have thirty-six.
On the thirteenth day, there is *uṣas*, that *citram* [hymn], one *veṣṭana*, and one [more];
twenty-two are for *prātarjita*; two for *vṛtra*; six for *aṣṭra*;
then *pūṣan*, twelve; then one *visruk* and one *ekanā*.

From the path, the seventeenfold [Stoma] has seven streams; from the fivefold, the tenfold has three streams; from the fourfold, the elevenfold has four streams; from the one, the twelvefold has two streams; from the four, the thirteenfold has one stream.
Thus the wise have declared.

On the thirteenth day, there are the Ghṛtavatī verses; from the wrapping, ten [verses] follow in sequence; nineteen for the Navadaśāhena; four and five for the two Sapatnā sections; the Ānāsatyā verses consist of nineteen; Trivita has six; and the Visrutā verses are twenty-six.
This Stoma is eighteenfold; in the sixth [day] there is one Vṛt;
with the Stomas on the fifteenfold [day], there are six Vṛts; with eight, there is the Ekata;
the thirteenfold is for long life and for splendor; the Śaya is single.
The twenty-fifth [verse] is not a protection; there is one [turn] of seven [verses] spread out.
When you have bound [it] with the sixteenth, and if the fourth is three times in two [places], then indeed the *utanohiḥ* is on the seventeenth, and the eleventh is wound three times.
The seventeenth [verse] belongs to Agni; twelve are renowned as being in three [groups];
the seven seers, nineteen, Vṛc, and four Visraps; six [verses] beginning with "uttiṣṭha brahmaṇas pate"; two in the Ṣolaśī; and Vṛt as the fifth, followed by Visruk.
"Pañcadaśī," "pranūnaṃtu," "ṣaḍviṣṭuk," "caikanāntakam," "viṃśati," "brahmaṇaspate," two "vṛtau," and three "visrutaḥ"—
thus [are the sections] in the Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
The thirty-third chapter of the *Padakārikāratnamālā* is completed.
Now begins the thirty-fourth chapter:
"O God, all [the worlds] on the twelfth day; the one that has grown, the three that are renowned."
To the distributor, seven; to the one who increases, two; to the far-famed, two; for the Brahman priest, twenty; four for the Vṛccha and one for each;
twenty for the dance, six for the Sūta, and likewise six for the Veṣṭana.
For Tapas there are twenty; for Saptavṛt, one is well-known;
from the rivers comes Pauñji with twenty; and for Ekādaśavṛt, ten;
for Sandhi there are twenty, where the fourteenth is the fifteenth.
Twenty [stanzas] are for the *utsādas*; nine *vṛtis* are proclaimed; from the *armas*, ten *veṣṭanas* and one [are derived] by twenty elephants;
for the wife (*bhāryā*), twenty-four [from] wood (*dārvā*); thirteen [are] three *visruks*.
The twenty-second [section] belongs to Ṛtastena; the twelfth is for Vṛddha, while the first is for Manyu.
Twenty verses are recited for Yama, and the fourth consists of ten verses and three triplets.
The twenty-third is for Yama, consisting of thirteen verses and three triplets.
From twenty-four *saras*, there are five; from eleven, one;
for *bībhatsā*, twenty-one; and eight for the two increases (*vṛddhī*), both being *visrut*.
For the king of twenty-four syllables, eleven; [and] three *visruts*.
Twenty [verses] for Pratiścutkāya, ten *vṛc*s and one *visruta* for Daśavraja;
eighteen for Marmāyat, six *vṛc*s and two *nāntaka*s;
twenty-two for Agni Pīvā, five *vṛc*s and one *visruta*.
Twenty-seven [syllables] for these [verses], eleven for the Ekādaśī, and nine for two [others].
Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter in the *Padakārikā Ratnamālā* on the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
Now begins the thirty-fifth chapter:
On the eleventh day [of the lunar fortnight] consisting of a thousand heads, there is the fourth [day]; the Puruṣa is indeed fourfold; here, on the fifteenth day, there is a pair, a pair, a pair.

In the fifteenth [syllable], there is this much [of the breath] for the two increases; in three and two [syllables], it is three-quarters; in the sixteenth, it is raised upwards; there are three and five emissions;
from that comes the Virāj; in the fourteenth, there are four, and for the sixth, there are six.

From that sacrifice, on the thirteenth day, three [offerings] were made for each of the three [periods]; or else, from that "all-oblation" (sarvahuta) sacrifice, one [offering] was made with three [verses].
From that, on the fourteenth day, the horses [were offered], one [offering] with five [verses] added. Then—
That sacrifice [is performed] on the fifteenth day; by four [verses] it is a *visruk*, and by one it is a *pañcadaśa*. When the Puruṣa is cut into three parts, one becomes one.
The Brāhmaṇa is its *pañcadaśī*; there are three *vṛts* and five *visruts*.
On the fourteenth day, the moon indeed flowed forth from eight [limbs];
from the navel on the fourteenth day, one [part] was formed by five [days] for two [limbs].
Since the Puruṣa was offered as a sacrificial oblation, fourteen [parts] and five [days] were the flowings.
On the fifteenth day there were seven; then on the two [subsequent] days of growth, six and two;
by means of sacrifice, eighteen sacrifices; four in the *visruk*;
from the nineteenth, nine were produced; six and three are declared in the *vṛc*.
On the ninth day, I am the Veda; on the tenth, Prajāpati; on the eleventh, eighteen; on the twelfth, one; on the thirteenth, five and one;
on the fourteenth, from the gods; and on the fifteenth, ten and thirteen.
Rucā, Brāhmā, and Ṣoḍaśī; Pañcaviṃś, Sruv, Vināntaka, Viṃśati, Draś, Lakṣmī, Catura, Dvaya, and likewise Ekanā;
then Agni on the eleventh, and Dvaya is chosen on the sixth.

All these [stomas] are on the fifteenth day; two turnings are released for two [days], and there is no counterpart for that; eight turnings, one released for each, twenty-two, this indeed four, and the turning on the fifteenth day.
The *venastá* consists of twenty-four [verses]; six times five and one;
twenty-four [verses] for the *pratadra*; four [verses] by two; the *sána* is one;
the *nandhúḥ* is seventeen; two and six and one.
*Parīto* [is recited] seventeen times; *ṣaḍvṛtaḥ* three times as a unity;
*paridyāvā* twenty-four times; for the four [verses], three as a unity;
*sadasaspatim* on the tenth [day]; *visruk* is praised once.
The *medhā* which was chosen on the fourteenth day— that pair and that other pair—
this [same] one is desired on the seventeenth day, and two others are chosen;
this [one] has departed with nine, while two are chosen and six have flowed away.
On the seventeenth day, there are five *vṛt* and seven *visruta*;
on the eleventh day, Vāyu purifies three *visruta*. By that [purification], there are ten *vṛt* and three *visruta*, but here there is one.
